(UPDATED REVIEW FOR OB64)
Paladins has been my favorite game of the last year, and still is, and I first played it on xbox console to level 70 and then am now level 19 on PC. My total hours are over 600. It is very deep with a high skill ceiling.  I am giving a slight positive review (JUST CHANGEG TO NEGATIVE - SEE REASON AT END) for the state of the game at at ob64, but it would have been an enthusiatic review at OB63 (Open beta patch number 63).  Overall, the the choice of hero, the gameplay, the five on five matches, the in-game adds, and now to a lesser extent now because of 0b64) card loadouts allow for endless replayabilty and challange.  The game is still worth playing for free, and  most will find it prudent to spend $30 to speed up your initial progress once you get a feel for it.
THE ELEPHANT IN THE ROOM - IS IT NOW PAY TO WIN (P2W) WITH OB64?
Yes - Ob64 also introduced the fact that you can make your cards stronger with real world money. Currently this is available only for legendary cards, but the path seems clear for them to implement this for all cards. I hope they do not do that.  There is now an endless progress grind for an overhauled 'unbound' card system. So they definately did introduce p2W, but only for the unbound mode.
DO I HAVE TO PLAY THE P2W UNBOUND MODE?
However,  there are ways to completely bypass the  p2W aspects by playing a 'bound' mode where you cannot use any card upgrades. This mode is in fact used for competitive play. They also gave us at OB64 all the cards unlocked which saves tons of time that it took at OB63.  New players have all the abilities in bound competive and casual mode that experienced players do.
WHAT DISADVANTAGE DO NEW PLAYERS HAVE?
New players havent yet learned how to play the heros, and this is where the $30 purchase comes in that I recommend. Rather then grind out the gold needed to unlock all 34 heros, get the $20 founders pack so and a booster pack so you get all the heros unlocked. THe booster pack agets you extra XP and cards/gold for a few weeks to jump start your progress. That is all the money I would say you should spend.
IS THE GAME STILL CUSTOMIZABLE AND BALANCED AT OB64?
The heros are constandly being balanced through patches so dont ever think you wont play a hero just becuase he is bad today. To get all 34 would take time or gold (in game currency) though. You can be very competive with about eight unlocked. Ideally, play them all at least to level four to learn their abilities so you can counter them with your favorite hero, as well as to get the chests to champion chests to unlock the cards for your favorite heros. At OB64 Hi-Rez trashed the popular and unique idea of a custom 12 pt balanced card loadout system, and by doing so ruined a really nice aspect of making it a custom experience. All cards now have set pts assigned. The cards variously affect the power of the four abilities each hero has, as well as other things like speed, hit pts, or anti healing against opponents. This also resulted in a unbalanced mess and many heros who were good are worse, and many who were average are better. Movement playstyles are gone, but new damage ones are possible, and additional legendary cards that focus on added damage were added as an option. Basically it is a completely new game at OB64.  Overall there are horrible balance issues though right now. The good news is that in future patches these should be more easy to fix since the ability to favor cards over others has been removed by loading htem with pts has been removed. Although HI-REx completely ignored its fans by removing the 12 pt system, they do have a good history of trying to balance cards. I feel they will balance the decks in future patches. However, I do think they should have kept the 12 pt system in place and instead just made that more balanced rather then trash it altogether. Regardless of how much Hi-Rez says this is hard to do, I agree with the community that they did not listen to us and did not try hard enough to make a 12 pt system work.
IF YOU CHOOSE TO PLAY UNBOUND HOW BAD IS THE GRIND TO UPGRADE CARDS FOR FREE?
Unbound mode right now against humans is pretty much even, as most folks dont have cards with advanced pt spreads yet. This will change and it wil be chaos soon. Occasionally I see someone with an 8 or higher card but that is about every fourth match. It is basically the same as bound mode, and the vast majority of players have level 4 cards or less. If you do decide you want to play unbound 'pay to win' mode you will want to upgrade your cards though, as you will get left behind. I fear a bit for new players in a month or two and have no idea how what they will think. You can currently get cards for free in a predictableand daily grind through 4 minute almost guaranteed win of the day matches against bot players. They better keep this shortcut in place or I am definately not recommending this game, because right now the grind to level up cards is insane by playing 50/50 win percentage ~12 min games against human oppenents. At least  the daily bot matches give you the equivalient of 34*7500 gold for free for 34 unique champion chests (if you played each champion once a day), including alot of legendary card upgrades as well, which seem to have a normal drop rate.  These champion chests give you cards only for the champion you just played with, so they are not as RNG as the Radiant chests, which give you random card upgrades across all 34 champions. So although the grind is bad, and especially bad for new players, you should be able to get all cards to around level 6 (out of 10) using this tip and be competitive without too much effort if you grind against bots, especially at least if you do it for your core heros each day.
HEROS AND TEAM COMP AND IN GAME ITEMS:
There are 34 heros and each match is a five on five match. You also have to learn the pros and cons of each hero and how they both compliment your team, but also counter your opposing team. This all has to be a bit relearned at OB64 due to the balance changes. There are obvious bad and good hero picks that are situational, as well as for the map itself. You should have nowledge of which card deck you want to pick once you see the others teams compostion. You can only do this once at the start of the game. Then, during the match, as it progresses you choose to further develop your character's abilities to run faster, or take less direct damage, or regen abilities faster, etc. Through a choice of four in-game items. Turn off auto purchase but remeber to try to buy extra in game items when you die. A sure sign of a noob is someone who doesnt buy in game items or buys the wrong ones.  There is little nuance here although not as much as in Smite.
CONCLUSION
I am giving it a positive even tough ob64 hurt it alot. Based on past attempts to balance the game, I feel Hi-Rez is committed to continue to balance the heros in future patches. Although they introduced some P2W aspects it isnt that hard to get the cards if you play daily against bots, and at least by  keeping an unbound free and compitive mode non P2W mode they allow everyone to be on 100% even abilities on day one.  The optional cosmetic skins are good and the core  gameplay overall is fun. Matches often can change momentum and a team losing 1-3 comes back and wins 4-3, so never give up.  You really don't have to spend anything to have a blast and be competive. You do need to commit a lot of time to learn all the heroes and play styles though. It is more challenging and deep than you might think at first.

So you're thinking of buying Cossacks 2?
Well do it. Sounds like Shia is writing this review but he wouldn't be wrong this game is awesome. The game is fun and user friendly and although dated I kinda still like the style. Now you may see many reviews saying stuff along the lines of "the first one was better" or "down with the patriarchy" ignore those. The only way to see whether or not you will like this game is to try it, go and pirate it and try the game out. Then, if you are a good person and like the game you can buy it.
Anyway on to the actual review.
The game itself is nice and has a bunch of different nations to chose from (being from the UK I play British) but there are many other good nations to chose from such as France, Poland, Austria, Spain, Rhineland, Russia and a bunch more! Each one has strengths and weaknesses, such as the British have great infantry and rifleman squads but lack great cavalry.
The game-play plays out like any generic RTS, build a base and all that until you realise you cant get all the resources yourself...
There are towns located across the maps that you must capture to gain the resources such as gold, food, iron and coal.
Without these you will lose, for example with no coal you will not be able to shoot. At all. So its rather important that you keep a stockpile and don't shoot unless you need to. The towns also make the combat more centralised which can lead up to some cool big battles.
The only gripe I have with this game is that the multiplayer is dead as it is an old game so unless you know some people who own it you will have to play single player which while fun for a while, you will bore after a while.
There is also a very limited amount of maps, and they can get boring after a while, especially if you are playing with multiple players as they are even more limited.
All in all I like this game and you should too (and if you don't its Obama's fault)

As a newcomer to the series, I had no idea what to expect from this title, and I was certainly surprised how deep this game went in seemingly all directions. There’s so much more than what you might see as a just another shooter with stealth mechanics. There is a very open-ended spectrum to how you can play this game: from core mechanics, to how you approach the levels and scenarios, to what decisions you make along the game’s satisfyingly lengthy narrative. Will play it stealthily or with guns-blazing? Will you go under, over, around, or through your enemies? Will you take your enemies down mercifully or lethally? Will try out all these things, whenever you feel like it? With this game, you certainly can, and I chose to use variety as I played through on the game’s Hard difficulty setting. And unlike many RPG-type games, you can play with variety and not really feel penalised for it or pidgeon-holed into a certain play style.
Although I did focus mainly on the stealth and hacking route, I was never afraid to pull out the guns when things got hairy, and I never really felt the need to choose the powerups relating to guns and the brute-strength approach. At any rate, it was highly enjoyable going into each of the games encounters, figuring out what approach I wanted to take and then using the right tools for the job to execute my plan. And when things didn’t work out as planned, it’s still fun enough to weasel your way out or simply re-load and try things differently.
I would insist people try to play this game more as a stealth game where possible, as that is what makes this game stand out. Most of the weapons feel quite good, but other, more high-profile and dedicated FPS games do it better than what can be found here. So if you’re looking for a gun-toting blast, this game certainly has elements of that, but it shouldn’t be the reason why you should play this game. A second qualm I have with the game would be the sub-par graphics, which are likely by-products of game development sprawled across a variety of platforms, but as a trade-off I guess you get a lengthy game with still quite detailed environments. Lastly, there are a couple signature moves the game has which the game doesn’t really capitalises on nearly enough, or provides enough obvious and enticing opportunities to use.
At the end of the day, when it comes to this Director’s Cut, you’re left with a great package with excellent value. This sci-fi romp delivers an experience which is far greater than the sum of its parts, and it’s all tied together with strong characters and a fantastic story that isn’t afraid to ask the big questions of humanity and progress.

It's definitely something you'll fumble with to start. Getting used to the touch pads takes some getting used to. The customization is also fantastic, albeit not perfect, but there's enough to tweak to really help make it an enjoyable and personal experience. And you can use it with non-Steam games too, so long as you add them to your Steam library.
Keep in mind, it's not something that will ultimately replace mouse and keyboard setups, but it works well enough if you set it up right. I don't use it for all games. Most FPS games I still stick with M+K, but with anything I'd normally use my XB1 controller, I've been using my Steam controller instead and it's been working excellently as a replacement for that. I feel I can get much more precision and versatility with the Steam controller over an XB360 or XB1 controller.
Overall, it's a fantastic little controller. Just be willing to give some time to get used to how it functions. Don't expect it to be your ultimate go-to for every single game, but it'll definitely prove its worth with many titles.

Red Orchestra is notable for its emphasis on realism in comparison to other World War II-based FPS games. The game takes place on the Eastern Front of World War II and covers the period from 1941 to 1945. The player is given the opportunity to participate in the reconstruction of events in the Red Army and also for the Wehrmacht. The game is targeted primarily at the network mode, but there is a single-player game against bots. Each location (map) is a really existing historic district. Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45 features an advanced ballistics system for both small arms and tank rounds - incorporating bullet drop, flight time, and tanks with more realistic armor properties than most games (featuring: penetration and deflection, in relation to range and projectile trajectory angle).

In a year of absolutely top-notch video games, this is my game of the year of 2017, by far. NieR: Automata proves that some stories can only be told through video games, and has the ability to shape the medium for a good time to come. Although at it's core it's a hack-and-slash, it effortlessly blends elements of shoot-em-up, twin stick, bullet hell, and platformer games into it (sadly the text adventure from the first game doesn't return). The multiple routes of the game that change after each playthrough keep it fresh and provide changes to the story that will keep you guessing. The game's music is without a doubt some of the best ever created for a video game, and absolutely lives up to the legacy the first game set back in 2010. Yoko Taro has excellent vision and his ability to tell a story is incredibly unique, and I hope he continues to make games for many years. If you haven't played this yet, I can only say: do it.

At first I was a little annoyed by the pricetag still being $60 9 months after the release, but now realise that it was worth every penny. The story is ♥♥♥♥ing amazing. Yoko Taro throws so many philisophical questions at you in a multitude of ways. Sometimes you don't even realize what he is doing to you until much later. The soundtrack for this game is great. I can't really say much about it without spoiling the story. The combat is enjoyable but pretty easy. Most definitely one of the best games I have played. 10/10.
It is also worth noting that the resolution bug still occurs so to make the game run in 1920 x 1080 you will need to either use borderless gaming or a community made patch. Honestly the lowered resolution isn't the end of the world, but having the extra pixels does make the game look a better.

Rampage Knights combines dungeon crawling beat 'em up action with looting, procedurally generated levels as well as rogue-like elements. Due to the random nature of the level generation process as well as the multiple character classes available the game offers a high level of replayability and is well worth its price of admission!

So, I'll start off by saying I waited for this game since I heard the day of it's leaks. I personally never played the older games, but as you know... their gameplay was pretty bad. Nier Automata takes a step up from that and they have improvised on a lot of things they failed to achieve in the older games. The older games were story rich and had outstanding stories, just as Automata does. Automata is my favorite singleplayer game of the year and it's definitely the kind of game that leaves that "feeling" in your chest after you complete it. You feel empty. Yoko Taro likes to punish us and leave us wanting more after the game is over.
Nier Automata is the kind of game that isn't for you if you've never played a story rich game before/don't care about the story. Do not play it if you don't plan to delve into the story. But there's something about Nier that most games failed to do for me; pull you in. Nier pulled me in from the very start of the game. You have so many questions from the start, and even at the end you still do. "What comes after?" is what I was always thinking.
The soundtrack. The soundtrack is hands-down the thing that makes the entire game. It's beautiful, absolutely stunning. I listen to the OST every chance I get and I even would buy their soundtracks/CDs if I had the money, just to support them. The music always manages to send chills down your spine combined with how well they fit into each part of the story perfectly. It's amazing, seriously.
The characters... boy. To avoid spoilers, you will grow attached to the characters. The characters in this game are very loveable. I started off hating A2, but as time went on, she grew on me and is now one of my favorite characters. 2B can come off as aloof, but it later on explains why and honestly that's what hit me so hard. I used to think 2B was a bad character/with bad design until I experienced all of the endings and went researching into some lore. 9S. God, don't even get me started. I love him. He's like my child. He has an A+++ English voice actor who did an astounding job portraying him and his emotions he felt throughout the entire game. Everyone I've talked to that's played this game will tell you that even if they do not particularly like him. He isn't my favorite character, but jeez, props to his English VA.
Cons... this game is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ without a controller. I recommend using one, any. I played this game with a Wii U controller (God, it was awful.) but it was better than playing with keyboard/mouse. Please play it with a controller. I cannot stress this enough. The other characters aside from mostly 2B/9S/A2 don't get much backstory, even then, A2 doesn't have much of a backstory unless you go researching into it. I think they could've done a better job with explaining the backstory of each of the characters, but that's actually really hard to do nowadays. It'd add more onto the game when you could simply just research it. But for those that are lazy, rip you.
That's all I can really think of, overall this game is amazing in it's own way and has a special place inside of my heart. I recommend this game to anyone that's involved in a story rich game/being a masochist. Oh, don't forget that controller. This game is actually awful without it.

So here's all I have understood so far.

If you graze enough bullets, you can activate a stronger shoot for a few seconds. If you are good enough, you can try to catch identical fruits to trigger a bonus (I don't know what it is yet since I haven't managed to do this).
Second part consists in you protecting trees by pouring water around them to extinguish fires created by thunderbolts, all this while avoiding fire things around and collecting fruits. You can refill water at the bottom of the screen.
I wouldn't say this is worth the price tag, yet if you can, give it a try (out of curiousity).

I really enjoyed the first one. It focused on being an experience rather than a game, and as a art project was a compelling experience with a cool romhack knockoff bible game aesthetic. It was an eclectic art project and experience, not a game, and it excelled at being what it was. This sequel has the potential to improve upon that formula but sabotages itself with brutal design choices.
In essence, this one is a earnest attempt at making a boss rush bullet hell shooter. It has bombs, a risk system, and bullet grazing, so on paper it's actually somewhat sophisticated. This is filtered through the bootleg bible game look of the first, and visually does the trick for me - it pulls off the aesthetic very well. However, it is brutally difficult and unforgiving - you'd actually have to excel at the genre to be able to progress in this one to any degree. One hit deaths and no checkpoints whatsoever, and there's a minigame between each boss with utterly broken mechanics. So if you wanted to take in this one like the first - as a trippy outsider art experience, you'd only be able to do so if you regularly play and excel at insane♥♥♥♥♥♥like DoDonPachi. And if that describes you, paradoxically you wouldn't be interested in playing a super low-rent version of it like this. Who is this for?
They made an art project and were told they should've made a game, so they made a game when they should've made an art project. I like the developer's other work, so this one is really disappointing.

This game is surprisingly fun. It's free, you should check it out for a bit.
The longer review:
The visual style is real good, turning on the "outline" option in the graphics settings is a must. The music is ... there? I suppose? It didn't really fit all the time, but the general background music wasn't typically intrusive. There are some strange hiccups here and there that seem like minor optimization problems. There are half second hangs every once so often, a bit of lag when changing zones, and some odd graphical pop-in in certain areas, but none of the issues are at all game breaking (or nerve grinding).
The combat feels a hair static (though that could just be my class). I would like for there to be a few more starting abilities, having 3 buttons for 10 levels is a bit boring (though that could just be my class once again).
Some of the systems in the game are a bit cryptic and require you to feel around a bit, for example: fishing had a little movie to explain how it worked, whereas crafting was "good luck lol." I sorted it out, but it wasn't intuitive or explained at all. The gear / leveling progression is just fine so far, it seems to go by pretty fast. The cash shop prices seem totally fine, but then I don't know the game's progression very well yet.
All in all, I'm only about 2 hours in, and I don't know if I'll get back to this game, but it's certainly worth checking out.

Too many, and to me at first, this seemed like an ordinary MMORPG. And it is up to a point. So why have I "wasted" over 240 hours as this review is being written, on this game?
That's not too easy to answer;
pretty much none of the characters have any voices at all, it's mostly text to read in which means the story (for me) is harder to keep on top of and not skip through it. Except for the introduction to the game, that was pretty good
Also, there's a certain degree of that f2p syndrome too. Once at high levels (say level 60 and above) the grind is very large. Moreover, quite a few players at this time have equipment only available on the shop. For real money. So, playing pvp without spending a penny is very hard indeed to stay on top of the competition.
Yet, I'm still playing to this day. I have two characters: a level 77 and a level 33 and grinding on both with dailys on the weekends. Why? Well, I still find it fun to play although of its flaws. But, those flaws aren't the game's fault. It's the genre's fault for building it up like that. And, most importantly, some of the nicest people I have met have come from this game. My guild is extremely kind, considerate and give encouragement (even outside the game world). I would have never met these grand people if it weren't for this game.
So, why do I keep playing? It's because I find it fun and others form up this grand experience. And it'a not everyday you hear a gaming community being overall nice and polite people, and actually builds onto an already good game. Especially with MMORPGs

This game is closer to software than to a game.  The game's primary purpose is to help people understand how guns work, instead of shooting them.  When you get a new gun, the game walks you through a series of "Games," each showing in detail the gun's assembly and mechanical properties.  The first stage simply demonstrates the weapon's field strip, and the second and third stages let you competely dismantle every piece of the gun, down to every last pin.  The fourth stage allows you to analyze the gun's mechanics with cross-sections of the gun firing at up to 50X slow-motion.  The last three stages are tests and practices of memorizing the gun's complete disassemble and reassemble.  I recomend this game to gun enthusiasts and/or future gunsmiths.

This is an okay game!
I think I'm just going to do a +/- here 'cause otherwise I'll be here all day.
SPOILERS!!!
[+]
- Architectural & environmental art direction: City Ruins and The Forest Castle especially are the stuff of my dreams
- The ambient tracks are on the same untouchable level of audio bliss as the no vocals version of Shadowlord's Castle Memory from the original NieR
- The regular machines' design is iconic and a far more stylistically fitting marketing tool than 2Butt
- Fuuun, fluid movement and basic platforming
-
fantastic, thematic usage of fanservice and innuedo (!?) that manages to create pathos which feels actually earned (!???)
- A2 inheriting 2B's purpose prompting a physical metamorphosis & 9S literal physical bonding with a part of 2B. Yes.
- All machines make me internally cry
- In spite of everything, A2 is the saving grace of this game when it comes to its androids. The way she carries herself and the effortless nobility she emanates coupled with this very understated rage boiling inside of her is just nailed to perfection. Such a freaking shame. Shoud have been the only protag.
- Ending E is honest, unapologetically sweet and heartwarming, achieving the expected meta excess. It leaves the game on a highly positive note.
- Wagon Emil in a comfy scarf
- Combat bracers ♥
- Japanese voice acting
- The game is infused with the usual charming sensivity that's prevalent in Taro titles
[~]
- The Weight of the World. I mean, Ending E almost manages to make it transcendental but it doesn't change the fact that when I heard the english version after my first playthrough I thought someone was playing a prank on me. Thankfully I feel like the near-laughter that the song brought out in me would be appreciated by the devs
- Combat. Fuuun but the incentive to explore gradually lowers. The potential for combos is there and while at first I felt prompted to test various stuff out during regular gameplay, in the second half of the game I stopped caring. The DLC provides fun testing grounds though, and the Debug Room I guess, but that's detached from the actual game.
- Good intertwining of gameplay & interface details with the narrative, something the previous game tried to achieve and it turned out better here, Still not as polished or cohesive as I would like.
- Character design is hit-or-miss. I'm not a fan of the moefication process both Drakengard and NieR have been subjected to. This is a way more stylish endeavor than D3, but stuff like the YoRHa heavy armor just looks awkward. The twins are ugly. The Operators look really cool though. Also not into the 2B craze at all.
[-]
- The Factory levels after the prologue. Even a Taro game didn't manage to bring the neccessary flavor in order to not make them boring obnoxious snoozefests gameplaywise.
- Devola & Popola. Can't believe I'm saying this but it's fact. Mostly because...
- All damn backstories (except maybe Emil's?) are told through text adventure format (if that) and I'm pretty sure the total time of all of them combined is shorter than Kaine's backstory. It's double funny because it just happens that my favourite characters were the biggest victims of this. It can be understandable for supporting characters, but A2?
- Second playthrough doesn't make sense in terms of what information it shares. I hoped this time around it would actually be properly executed, but no. 9S' route just so happens to show the machines' perspective even when it's not prompted by him hacking into their cores. Okay. It's also a slog to get through since the majority of the playthrough is the same.
- 2B is just a sacrificial blood doll love interest. 9S has some intense personal drama going on so he's not as boring, but generally they're not the most captivating protagonists, and their early dynamics feel banal.
- I finish side-quests and bear witness to both androids starting to express understanding or pity towards machine lifeforms and then their perspectives completely regress into full-blown anti machine talk during main story, without a hint of self-awareness.
- Dumb in-game fanservice. I appreciate the devs had enough sense to not pollute the actual visual narrative with it (no unnecessary camera behavior during cutscenes etc.). I don't like 2B's antics, mostly the self-destruction & the achievement (Lollipop Chainsaw already did that one first anyway, and it was far more fitting and amusing than here). Also I was convinced they left A2 alone, besides her figure and outfit, but even that has the most uninspiried, skimpier version during her berserk mode. Make it interesting, you cowards. You can make legitimate nudity look cool and interesting if you just
. Everything is possible >:(
- The android side of things, in retrospect, is like...really flaccid (HEH!!!). I didn't much care for them with few exceptions. That's terrible.
NieR: Automata is a decent action rpg. Its gameplay becomes stale over the course of the game, but the story gets gradually better. If you've never played anything from Yoko Taro, this is a good start. It's possible that it will discourage you from checking out his and his team's more interesting works, though.
Oh also, this game is totally a master emotional manipulator, so regular users of the aforementioned term should stay clear. (I'd also recommend to stop consuming media in general but I digress).

It's a great game but a heavily flawed one due to the quality of the port. DSfix fixed almost every issue dark souls had except for the performance. Nier's equivalent: FAR still doesn't completely fix the crashes and freezes and the game still stutters due to the limitations of its tech. It wouldn't be much of a problem if the game had an autosave, but it doesn't. And with these crashes feeling seemingly random it's incredibly offputting to try and explore hidden areas for better loot only to crash and lose 15 minutes of progress.
Performance is ok on my gtx 970 and r5 1600. Very gpu demanding but light on cpu usage. Without tweaking global illumination using FAR you'll have a rough time holding 60fps. but as mention before it might just be limitations with the tech itself. As the game tries to hit 60 on ps4 but has a hard time in certain spots, even on the pro. Since the game is designed to be played best on a controller minor drops aren't too noticable, but areas like the starting city have A LOT of stutter which IS noticable even on a controller.
When the game works you have an exceptionally stylish game that oozes charm. the soundtrack is amazing, probably the best out of any game i've played in the last few years. The combat is the platinum speciality, if you liked bayonetta or MGR you'll love this. And beyond the platinum style fighting yoko taro makes sure to let you know that this is his game as fights constantly change camera angles and playstyles. The very first area of the game puts you in 3 different types of isometric shooters, before finally throwing you into platinum's beat-em-up game. There's a bossfight about 3 hours in that just turns into a straight up bullet hell almost seemlessly. It's amazing and throughout all of it I was grinning like an idiot.
Also 2B is a big tiddy goth GF. if you like platinum/yoko taro games, weeb trash or generally well made games give this a shot. it goes on sale relatively frequently (except during a christmas sale for some reason). If you're worried about performance the city area near the beginning is the roughest, you should be able to get there within 2 hours so if you aren't satisfied by that point with its perfomance you have the option to refund. Squenix has all but dropped support it seems and FAR development has ended/hit a brickwall for fixing the game's biggest problems so waiting for performance to get better isn't going to do anything.

Dead Rising 3 for PC... A misfit port at the start, and an overwhelming game at the finish.
Don't get me wrong, this is a good game, but the port to PC had its fair share of problems. But those are all in the past now, and there are plenty of easy fixes for the few that remain, so I'll just say this: This is a good game IF you have a good computer.
My last computer, which I first bought this game on, wasn't all that bad. I can't remember the specs, but suffice to say, it was a good laptop for the most part. But this game was too much for it. The frame rate issues were so severe that the game ran as slow as a zombie, pun intended. Yet I still played this to the point that I beat the final boss and completed the story. But it wasn't very pretty...
But now that I've got myself a new computer, with better specs from the looks of it, the game runs just fine. Maybe it was just my old computer that couldn't handle the game, or maybe Capcom's hotfixes worked as they should in the end? In either case, now I can enjoy this game as I should have a few years ago.
Since this is the third entry into the DR-series, I'm pretty sure we're all familiar with the basic premise: Grab anything you can find and beat zombies with it, rescue people and kill psychos. It's all pretty standard, except you really can pick up anything, from bricks and broken pipes to garbage cans and benches; if it's not nailed down you can pick it up and use it as a weapon. That's the big selling point of this franchise as a whole, and I have to say, it's a good point.
With the second entry came the ability to combine different weapons into new and better versions, so how could this be improved on? Why, vehicles of course! The first two games had some vehicles to throw around, but it was all pretty limited between different zones. But now that the whole game is one big map, save a few special locations, there's no better time to introduce combo vehicles! Sure, there are only ten of them, but any one of them can lay waste to hundreds of zombies and make travelling the city a breeze! Normal vehicles aren't bad either, but there's just something more satisfying about riding a giant creepy clown cart which sucks up zombies like a vaccum and tosses small explosives than just... mowing them down with an SUV.
Oh, and there's a story about escaping the city with your buddies before a big bomb goes off. But who cares about the story? Just have fun and get out in due time.
Frankly, these are some of my favourite kinds of games: They don't care about story, they don't care too much about characters or even realism, they just put you somewhere and lets you have a wild ride. It's like Doom: You're fighting demons on Mars, what else do you need?
I can drone on and on about the different things you can do, the fun possibilities of dressing up in women's lingerie and then beat zombies to (permanent) death with a handbag, or with a giant battleaxe, or a lightpost that can fry, freeze or electocute your foes. But frankly, you're best off to find those things for yourself; provided you have a good computer of course.
So yeah, I can recommend this one to the well equipped gamers. Now if you'll excuse me, I still have a few achievements to earn and a few more zombies to kill. Ta-ta!

I got my Steam Controller today, and was not disappointed.
The boxing was pretty and solid. It took me almost a full minute to unbox due to the fact that I was taking very careful care to peel off the stickers, to not damage the box. Eventually, I got the box open. The controller's plastic felt a bit cheap, but regardless, the design was pretty.
It took me a moment to read over the quick-start guide, before I plugged it into my computer. The moment it was ready to use, I launched Big Picture and updated my controller. It took a few tries in wireless mode, but eventually it connected and updated.
The first game I played with a Steam Controller was Team Fortress 2. The first few moments was awkward aiming and wrong button presses, but after a few hours, I managed to get the hang of the basic controls. True, my performance, compared to mouse and keyboard was worse, but it's a controller, what do you expect? The buttons are all in easy-to-reach places, and overall, the controller is comfortable to use.
One complaint is that the triggers are not sensitive enough. I prefer tap-triggers, not ones I have to pull all the way. It's led to a lot of failed shots in TF2.
As this is just day 1, I will update my review as time goes on. But so far, I am very happy with my controller.
Let Steam Controller Boot Camp begin.
EDIT: It's been a while since I got my steam controller, and I love it so much. It's great for games like Dark Souls, allowing a level of precision on the trackpad that normal analog sticks cannot do. However, I do have one complaint that the left D-Pad needs to be made so you stop accidentally hitting the wrong button. I press the middle of the Up button, for example, and sometimes, if I don't press absolutely straight down, I end up hitting left or right. This game is a perfect old time rts. Cossacks 2 bfe has all what a strategy loving player needs. You have fast economy (building your base in 10 minutes). Massive battles with over 5000 units!!! Perfect tactics, units have formations, morale, stamina.
Realistic terrain tactics, like trees make you lose accuracy, you cant shoot over building (only artillery), standing on highland increases the range of your units, units can lose formation and be forced to flee. Each unit can either shoot and reload or fight melee.
Realistic economy, shooting is based on resources, you have to have coal to reload. Units can die if you have no food. To get resources you have to defeat and control villages, resources are delivered by mules which gives another tactical advantage.
Overall i rate this game 8/10 because it is military/tactic focused. Graphic has practically no requirements. Gives you massive battles and lots of tactical possibilities.
Minus:
Single player - AI is plain stupid
Multiplayer - very few players
Buy this game, and tell your friends to buy it too, get more players because this game is worth saving!

Go! Go! Nippon! ~ My First Trip to Japan ~ is a cute little visual novel, where you explore many of the most famous landmarks in Japan, in the company of Two sisters you befriended online and whom you stay with during your weeklong visit. Awkward situations arise, giving this game the feel of an anime, and as you explore more of Japanese culture and learn about it's history, your relationship with your new friends develops as well. All in all, it was a very cute game, with some funny dialogue and a couple of situations that gave it an anime feel. I thoroughly enjoyed the game, even though the playthrough was very linear. You can make some choices as to where you want to visit; However, a large part of the playthrough will be visiting specific areas in Japan, such as Kyoto. I don't regret picking this game up in the slightest and would like to see a sequel even, to further explore Japanese culture and history, as well as to continue to character development and relationship between the Protagonist, and the sister.

I normally don't write reviews but for Go! Go! Nippon! ~My First Trip to Japan~ I just feel like I have to.
Before I start I have to say that I am normally not the kind of person that enjoys Visual novels, at least not for long.
But this one has really funny conversations that just tingle my sense of humor. The characters are well chosen and I have to say it makes it more interisting for me that there are only 3 characters.
And one other feature that stands out here is that you learn alot about Japan.
So I would like to recommend this game to you if you:
1. Want to learn a little bit about Japan while having fun.
2. Want to play something funny and interesting.
Although I have to say that it's just my own opinion, other might think differently.

It's worth it if it's on sale and you enjoy experience gameplay, but this is definitely not arcade fun.

I decided to make a review for DR3 in light of the announcement of DR4.  I want people to first remember DR3 before getting hyped about DR4.
I'm a crazed super-fan of Dead Rising who has played unhealthy amounts of DR1, DR2, and DR2-2.  I actually see the mediocre performance (that many people have complained about) as a minor issue compared to the fact that every little nuance that made Dead Rising special was altered to be worse for DR3.  DR3 is a pretend Dead Rising that lacks the cohesion and fun of the previous games.  The only people I would even recommend this game to are people who are not fans of the series.
Forgive me if I forget to mention any terrible garbage about DR3 as I haven't played it in a few years.
A lot of people don't like the time mechanics in DR so I will just point out how it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ regardless.  They didn't just remove the time.  But rather, they made the time so generous that it is basically meaningless.  The time management fun of DR1 is gone, so they might as well have left it out.  The time in DR3 is just a pointless parody of the time in the old games.
Remember the fun of knowing particular spots to get specific items for a situation?  Doesn't really matter anymore.  You can just spawn an infinite number of items from a locker (balanced only with a generous cooldown).  You do have to go to a safe house to use a locker though (safe houses are conveniently located everywhere).  But to double down on the pointlessness, you wont even be using normal items (besides guns) because you will only be spawning the most effective combo weapons.
More is not better.  DR3 pushed the amount of zombies on-screen without factoring in things like fun or performance.  The amount of zombies in DR3 reminds me of late game DR1&DR2 (you know, the least fun parts of those games).  No locations in DR3 really feel more dangerous or more safe.  There is just a butt ton of zombies everywhere, always.
A lack of strategy is probably what you could boil most of my complaints down to.  It's all ruined.  Gaining knowledge of locations/effects/dangers/etc, prioritizing missions, setting goals, being creative while planning your load out . . . etc. etc.  All of it, ruined.
Didn't really know where to fit vehicles in, but they suck too.
In the old games, the car's location, durability, and token safety from zombies were important factors.  Not in DR3.  You can just spawn turreted vehicles like you can items.  Not that you would want to drive the vehicles as you usually get out due to the roadblocks every 10 feet.  Also, the zombies trigger a constant stream of QTEs (we love those right?) whenever you are driving a car.
Jesus I'm being negative.  I can't help it.  DR1 is maybe my all-time favorite game.  I'll try to end with something positive about DR3.  Uhhhhhhpffffffffshhhh . . . I guess it's nice to pick items up while moving?

Deus ex: Human Revolution is an amazing dark and gritty FPS set in the dystopian future of 2022 where humans are divided on how they feel about the new augmentation technology. Augmentations allow humans to rise above their limitations by being able to do things such as react quicker, run faster, or jump higher among many other things. The story focuses on an ex-swat turned private security director, Adam Jensen, for Sarif Industries, a major biotech corporation. Because of a discovery that was made at Sarif Industries a team of highly augmented mercenaries attacked their headquarters and killed the team responsible for the discovery making sure that it would never reach the light of day severely injuring Adam. As a result of his injuries Adam had to be heavily augmented against his will to keep him alive. With his new found abilities it is up to Adam to track down those responsible for the deaths of the scientists and to find out the truth about what really happened that day. The player has the ability to choose how Adam goes about a situation being able to choose between dealing with enemies passively or lethally which changes the way characters address him. With multiple endings the game offers many choices for the player to make that affects the story. Overall, the game poses a question that can be applied to science even today a decade before the game takes place which is should humans play god and it is up to the play to choose where they stand for themselves based on what they see throughout the game.

Cossacks II is a good game. I believe I'm in the minority when I say this, but I oh so strongly believe it.
Compared to the original Cossacks video game, it's distinctly different. The visual style, gameplay/gamefeel, and even the setting are radically different from Cossacks: The Art of War. It's not hard to see why fans didn't like this one or it's vanilla version. But if you really give it a chance and look at it as a nonsequel, you may see a very good game in it.
For those not in the know, the overall series has features like troop morale, limited ammunition for gunpowder weapons, commanding and management of troop formations, and a visual style that invokes the image of paintings from the era coming to life. It's an extreme different game from say, Age of Empires or Total War, despite the simularities. The learning curve is slightly higher than those games aswell. Battles are often stalemates that have to be broken through concentrated attacks, flanking, and clever usage of terrain features.
This game is more or less dead and its developer, GSC Gameworld (Who is known more as the team behind the STALKER franchise of FPS games), is in a state of pseudo non-existance. But please, buy this game. It deserves more love and attention!
Add me if you want to play multiplayer sometime, I would greatly appreciate that.
And for anyone who disagrees with me on the games quality, come on, at least it's not as bad as Napoleon: Total War...

Paladins is one of the best competitive FPS games I've played in my life and I've been gaming since 1984.
I cannot heap enough praise on this game. Sure it's got its annoyances like terrible team balancing (though it's been improving) and horrible map rotation (my god why is it always Fish Market and Hidden Temple!?) but at its core Paladins is literally my favorite competitive FPS title since Counter-Strike.
The sheer variety of the play is absolutely amazing. Every time I start to get even slightly bored with the game, I try a new Champion and it's like I'm playing an entirely different game. The strategy involved is staggering when at first blush it seems like there might not be that much. Right from the character select screen you're tasked with making sure that you have a balanced team and the fact that you've got less than 20 seconds to do so makes it even more intense. If you don't play as a team, you're done for and where with other games that might be a death sentence with random players on a team, suprisingly the online community is fantastic and most players are fully willing to work together. The game is also great for new players or veterans alike with the huge variety of champions to choose from (30+ at the time I write this) and where at first you might think that you love one class like Frontline, you may be suprised to find that you play incredibly well with a complete departure from your normal.
My friends and I always joke that in DND (and most video game RPGs) I can only play as a Barbarian. Tanks are my bread and butter. After falling in love with Ash and pushing her to level 9, on a whim I decided to try Maeve, the most irritating Flank champion I had ever encountered in the game. At first I just died constantly but after a few matches, I started really falling in love with her speed and grace. Now she's my all time favorite champion and the character that I usually main; but it didn't stop there. Seris is freaking spectacular as a Support - this is literally the first time in a game I've felt empowered playing a healer - and Willow is really fun as a damage.
Amazingly enough, even though there are a few champions who feel a little OP compared to others at first glance, the game is incredibly well balanced. I thought Vivian was ridiculously OP at first but after playing against her a bit more (and a slight nerf by the devs), I discovered she's not as bad as I originally thought, she just requires a different strategy. The same can be said for all of the champions. They can all be incredibly deadly in the right pair of hands and totally useless in another.
All in all, Paladins is MY game. It's so much fun!  It's well balanced and it's fair (no pay to win). If you haven't tried this game yet, you really don't know what you're missing. I can easily see myself still playing this game 10 years from now. Seriously, I love it that much!

Unlike most of Steam, I actually enjoyed the first Uriel's Chasm. It was a nice mixture of game styles with a very avant-garde approach to tying them all together, and the drug-addled/fever dream christian themes and blasphemy had me asking "what the ♥♥♥♥" on more than one occassion. So when Uriel's Chasm 2 was announced, I was excited to play it.
The above footage was recorded while I had a cold (hence the bad volume levels, I forgot to check them before hand due to how loopy I was from the meds) and wound up lost to time until I found it the other day. I played it again once more after that, and the feelings are about the same. As a bullet hell, it still works out in a Titan Quest sort of way. Just one boss fight after another with the theme of fruit. It's a bit confusing there as they cause pain in the bullet hell sequence, but then in the strategy segment to stop the trees from burning they are required to advance, making them beneficial.
Unfortunately, I have not been able to complete the game, so I'm not really sure how or if a lot of these elements play into each other, but from what I experienced it all just seemed to be random things thrown together in more of a religious overtone. Part of the reason for this is both a lack of skill on my part, as well as a lack of anything to really keep me going. Unlike the first, this is just the same two games back-to-back. There is another in the trailer but I haven't seen it played, nor did I reach them.
The lack of a continue screen is also a shame. If you die, you go straight to the beginning. No contrinues, no second chances. Your hit counter also doesn't seem to change other than you get one when you start a new boss battle (I think, that's what it seemed from when I played). There's also small Sega CD style compressed video of what looks like an abandoned parking garage that seems to have little to do with the game itself other than aesthetic. Rail Slave Games (the developer) continues to play these games off like a bad rom hack of a lost game, and things such as the Pac-Man fruit play into it as well. Sadly, it isn't necessary, nor does it really help anything.
Where the first entry had enough "what the ♥♥♥♥" moments level after level to keep the player invested to see what's coming next, this one just doesn't. And that's the fatal flaw in its design. This is ripe to set up a drug addled fantasy world of spiritual context, but the development team just don't take advantage of it. Hopefully their next entry (which I saw was something actually called 'Fever Dreams') will play into the strengths it is named after.

Absolutely amazing, maybe one of the best games this year if not this decade.
The theme of the story about what it truely means to be a human and why we feel emotions and can something 'created' as a robot eventually learn these emotions. Multiple endings is a great selling point which makes giving multiple playthroughs a must. The first playthrough being highly emotional and straight forward, but the second third fourth and eve fifth playthroughs are really what show a difference in perception, story and gameplay.
Now for the gameplay, my lord its 10/10. As of writing this review, I've just finished the game.  And all I can say is:
Wow.
In my entire 14 years of playing video games, I don't think I've ever seen a game quite like NieR:Automata.
The gameplay is so fluid and varied that you almost never feel bored.
The soundtrack is so atmospheric and really lends to the mood (especially at the end).
The characters are so well designed that you develop deep attachments to many of them.
The 2B booty is so amazing that you'll always have something to keep you entertained through the rare boring parts.
And the story...
Let me make this clear.  The story is THE BEST story I have EVER experienced IN MY ENTIRE LIFE.  What seems like a copy-and-paste JRPG story about saving the world turns into a really deep and shocking story that is impossible to truly describe without straight up spoiling the plot and its many twists and turns.
If you look past the terrible PC port (fixed with the FAR mod, look it up to fix this game on pc), you're left with a game that  is not only deeply satisfying, but also extremely innovative.
I'm usually hard to keep entertained when it comes to games.  In the past year, I've bounced from game to game, and only fully completed like one game.  This game was one of the few games that not only kept me enthralled, but also made me WANT to finish it.  The only other recent game that made me WANT to finish it had to be Dark Souls III, and that was through sheer masochism.  NieR:Automata has made me want to complete more of the games I have, to see where these games go and what they have to offer.
If I haven't made it abundantly clear, I gave this game a chance, and I loved it.
I hope that you will too.

This is another one of those games that look much worse than they are fun.
Even when a friend of mine recommended it to me, I was worried it might be trash.
As you might have guessed, it's not.
Rampage Knights is an "Isaac-like" brawler with a heavy emphasis on melee combat.
The dungeon is randomized every run and you can even bring a friend and play together online (and on equal terms with none of that half-baked "supporter" crap other games tend to do).
You can unlock higher difficulties, additional game modes, and a ton of achievements.
The latter aren't just for show though, as they do unlock new classes, characters, hats, and even permanent boosts, making them worth the time and effort required to unlock (most) of them.
Combat is fast paced and varied enough to keep you engaged for many hours.
You charge, dash, jump, dodge-roll, kick and stomp the crap out of ugly-looking monsters at delicious 60fps.
Be warned though, because the game has a tendency to screw you over in ways that are just blatantly unfair.
There were times when my character was knocked down right next to a bomb, causing me to get hit when I got up.
Another time the game made me respawn right on top of a set of spikes, and with no invincibility whatsoever, causing me to get hit (a friend of mine even respawned on top of a hole, killing her instantly). Some treasure chests are deliberately placed next to pits, dropping you to your death if you happen to fail the unlocking minigame.
It's moments like these that create hilarious situations in multiplayer, but in solo play they feel like a kick in the groin.
Speaking of multiplayer, I highly recommend playing it with a friend.
Just keep in mind that there is friendly fire, and while you don't take damage from each other's attacks (bombs excluded), you can still knock the other player into a pit, some spikes, or an explosion. Make sure to use voice chat so you can yell at each other properly.
If 12€ is too much for you, put it on your wishlist and get it when it goes on sale.

The foundation is there though. There is a character screen with multiple characters and customization, voice packs, progress and levels are saved between servers (No Idea how frustrating it was otherwise) and the base gameplay is there.

There is also a different section of other things such as: Bones, cars and AFVs. When I first tried this game I thought that since its free, it would be sh*t, but after only a few minutes of playing I found that it actualy is a very good simulator/teaching tool. This game has been very beneficial to me, in helping me understand everything about guns and all kinds of different guns, for when I fully enter my career and now have a huge leg-up. I also have now started designing and thinking about making proto-types of firearms of my own design. Overall I would strongly recommend this game, and will actively play this game for a long time to come.

The game is a lot of kill satisfaction. I was a bit disappointed that it wasn't quite as spooky as the original Doom or Doom 3, but the gameplay is very smooth and the combat is well done. You're forced to stay on the move, and your weapon loadout is actually relevant, as different weapons can be more effective on different monsters. The secrets and easter eggs are great. The story is meh, so if you're looking for an action-packed game with an engaging story go play Undertale.
My only gripes with the game are as follows:
- The clipping can be pretty bad. For a game that's been out this long, I'm surprised it's as bad as it is. There were a handful of times where I fell through the floor and died, or got stuck on a stair.
- Difficulty spikes. A lot of this game is fighting waves of monsters until you've killed them all. Sometimes those waves are much more difficult than others.

I find myself having a little bit of trouble on whether I would recommend this game or not, although this is definitely not a bad game by any measure, I just don't quite see how it is as good as the ratings, and other reviews seem to indicate. (See the bottom of this review for a TL;DR)
So, I will attempt to give as unbiased an opinion of this game as I can, by category to make it easier.
First is the gameplay: I have to say that the gameplay is good in the fact that is offers you an array of options to choose from with any given situation, you can either go in all guns blazing, or go sneaking around all stealthy, or find a balance between those 2 styles. I liked the fact it gave you the freedom in this regard. However, to be honest, I just didn't really find the combat particularly fun, I'm not quite sure why, perhaps it was the whole switching out between first and third person shooters that did it. Unlike other games, I never really felt like a badass while taking bad guys down, and I felt the combat is a little unforgiving (I was playing on normal difficulty) but given that stealth is an option that is acceptable because otherwise the stealth approach would be a little less inviting. In terms of how the stealth mechanics play out, I thought they were quite well executed, when you keep your wits about you, you can slowly, but surely make your way past pretty large groups of bad guys, but if you trip up you may find yourself forced into a fire-fight, but that is how a stealth game should be, so that is not a problem. Additionally, I thought the hacking mini-game was extremely well done, unlike many hacking mini-games (such as Mass Effect 1 or 2) it is not tedious and boring and you enter into it thinking "uh...better hack this damn terminal..." The hacking mini-game in Deus Ex requires some planning, strategy and quick thinking, the hacking mechanic was masterfully implemented.
Player Progression: Player progression is pretty good in this game, without going into any spoilers, you get xp points in which you can upgrade both passive, and active abilities at a reasonably regular basis, you can also buy xp for credits at certain stores. the game has a pretty extensive amount of upgrades and I think you would be hard pressed to upgrade all your abilities by the end of the game, this is good because it forces you to make decisions on prioritising upgrades for what your play-style is, for example: do I upgrade my stealth vision or do I give myself more armour? However, the amount of xp you get is not too prohibitive, you don't get so little xp you are forced to do go down one tree and you are stuck there, you can branch out over several ability trees to suit your style, just not all of them. The game seems to have plenty of weapons and items, and introduces them at a rather nice pace, you don't get 1/3rd of the way through the game and find you have already unlocked all the guns like some games, you get new guns right up until the end. In terms of purchasing equipment, it's a pretty standard RPG kind of set up; you do quests, loot various things, sell items off at stores, you get credits for it, you can then buy various upgrades, ammo and weapons at stores. Stores...*shudder* i'll open that bag of worms later in thie review.
Interface and Navigation: This games interface is quite nice, it has a nice high-tech feel to it and is rather well done, apart from one aspect, Navigation. The navigation in this game is horrible, although you have a map, it is never really useful for telling you where to go, the map is made up of un-detailed blocks that don't show you anything of the terrain or buildings in the area, so you don't know where to go to get to where the quest marker is. Remember that can of worms about shops I mentioned earlier? yea, here it is, sure, this game has shops, but they are NEVER marked on your map, you can only find them by remembering where they are, and given how useless the map is, and how the city hubs all look quite similar, it's damn tricky to remember, it also gives you no indicators as to where other points of interest are, such as your apartment.
Sound design and soundtrack: I know not everyone is as concerned with these two things as I am, but for those few who are; the actual sounds in this games sound design seemed pretty good, but they always seemed somewhat delayed by a few miliseconds, like, I would fire my gun, but it didn't quite match up with the muzzle flashes, perhaps it was just my imagination, or perhaps not. The soundtrack for this game served its purpose, it created the desired atmosphere, so I guess thats a plus, but it didn't really do much more than that. The soundtrack isn't bad but don't expect any amazingly epic soundtrack orchestrated moments.
Plot: Now, plot is a big part of this game. It's hard for me to be to critical of this games plot because, I can't really find anything wrong with it...but at the same time, I just didn't really find it all that engaging. It has everything one wants from a plot, a good concept, decent lore and an interesting world in which it is based in, some good plot twists, revelations...but...it just never seemed to get me particularly engaged in it, sure, there were a few moments where I was like :o but only a few. In all truth though, now that I think of it, there isn't anything wrong with the plot, but the characters. The characters all seems so two-dimensional, even the character you play as seems like he has no personality at all, he just seems like a bit of a robot, I guess, perhaps if that's how you wan't your character to be thats great, but I don't. I personally don't like his voice actor, he seems like he's trying to do some kind of forced batman voice most of the time, and he never shows any expression or emotion in his voice, there was only one point in the game where the character actually had any kind of decent voice acting. As for the other characters, the only one I came remotely attached to was the chick who flys you around in a helicopter, at least she had a little bit of personality. As for villains, they seem a little basic and somewhat generic for villains, theres nothing about them that really makes you think "gee...that guy actually has a point?...is he/she really the villain I have been led to believe?" Perhaps I have just been spoiled by the characters from games like Mass Effect and Starcraft II, but I just didn't really connect with any of them.
Graphics: For a 2011 game, they seem about what you would expect, nothing really good or bad about them.
Bugs/Issues: I did have issues with my screen flickering white until I turned the game to direct X 9 rather than using 11, which is somewhat unfortunate because I would have liked to get the benefits of using DX11. I also got low frame-rates in few-second bursts every now and then, and my system can more than handle this game. I have a hunch that you probably are safe from the screen flickering issue on an AMD graphics card, given that this game seems to be optimized for it, but it should still run fine on any Nvidia card.
All in all (A TL;DR/Summary): This is a decent game with a few different gameplay styles to choose from, it has pretty standard and character progression that is neat in the fact that it forces you to chose a play-style. it has pretty standard sound design and soundtrack. It has a nice interface but has terrible navigation. It has a very interesting world in which it is based and an intruiging plot, but is let down by rather two-dimensional characters.
My final verdict: Do I recommend this game? well...it honestly depends on the price, and the full $19.99 listed here, I would have to say no, however If it is on special, say $10.00 or under It might be worth picking up, if nothing more I will keep you occupied for a good 20-30 hours.

What can I say about NieR Automata that hasent already been said by now? NieR is a flawless example of why games as a medium can be art in their own right. The story at play here is so beautifully natural. The world feels real, and the story drip feeds itself out at a perfect pace. Combat is smooth and insanely fun. The boss fights are what you'd expect from a platinum game, spectactular and over the top. NieR's story is by far the best part of the game. Its a game that not only has a very strong and meaningful story to tell, but you can really sense the time and effort put into it. Its eerie how well this game works.
The use of sound in this game has to be commended. Sound design is such an underappreciated part of games, but in NieR, it was executed fantastically. The ambiance truely captures that loniness and heavy nature, but its not oppressive. All too often games fail to find that balance, but NieR accomplishes it in conjunction with the visuals. Its completely surreal to walk through the abandoned city ruins, nothing but the echo of your own footsteps and the ambiance. Often times I'd take breaks from the action just to appreciate the world that was constructed. It only adds to the story, and the deeper concepts and elements to the individual characters as well as the plot. The way characters interact, how they react and the tones feel very genuine. As a voice actress myself, I truly appreciate when roles are performed so well. When we as humans try to sound synthetic, it tends to sound bad. But here, the characters are allowed to fit their voices. They sound human, further adding to the questions like "What does it mean to be human". The way the sound, art style, world and mechanics all come together to form a very genuine feeling world. It immerses you and keeps you there. The game is very clever, with twists and turns that always keeps you on your toes. There's a charm to this game that is genuinely hard to describe.
Of course the game is not all gloom and melancholy. this is again where the sound design comes into play, and I cannot stress how truly good it is. The music, and how its implemented is executed flawlessly. Emotions like Hope, Loss, Loneliness, and Serinity all being portrayed by one track is impressive. There's a definite weight to parts, and at other times it feels lighter. For me, I received an almost benevolant tone from parts of the sound design. The sense that Life goes on, despite the wills of Machine and Android alike. The game makes you think. It's definitely got a philosophical tone to it, and whilst it may not appeal to everyone, I certainly enjoyed it and commend it. Many times games will try their hand at deep concepts, but rarely does it pay off in such a rewarding way. It only makes its success in NieR that much more satisfying.
In terms of mechanics the game was very agreeable. The combat mechanics are smooth and precise, and definitely rewards players with fast fingers and a nack for dodges. Much like Bayonetta, another of Platinum's successful series, NieR's combat is frantic and sometimes confusing. It pays dividends to learn to use sound as well as memorize timing to keep track of the enemies attacks coming at you. The Plug-In chip mechanic, as well as the games unique save feature further add to the immersion, and whilst hacking is a very efficiant means of attack, I found that it was difficult to get used to as the mouse likes to twitch the cursor around, but its not the hardest thing to get used too. I found by about 2 hours in I was hacking more and more reliably. All in all, sound mechanics overall.
One thing that must be commended is that despite this game being open world, I found that I never felt like any of the quests were slogs or chores. Often times a simple side mission would introduce a new idea or thought for the player to ponder. I remember several quests that caused my emotions to get tugged on. NieR is the only game that's managed to squeeze genuine emotion from me, actually getting me to cry pretty hard. This game is certainly an eccentric piece of work, and despite my constant flow of praises, I dont think its a game for everyone. Its certainly a game I feel everyone should at least try, but I find its a game that definitely deserves its accolades and praise.
The only thing that lets this game down is the port. Its pretty bad if I'm perfectly honest. The game does suffer frame rate issues and mechanics like hacking as mentioned above, suffer as they were clearly designed for the PS4, and suffer on the PC. There's also the issue with the Full Screen glitch that produces a black border around the game regardless of what resolution you're set to, and the occassional quest not loading correctly, but this was rare and only happened a few times for me. The PC would have been a fantastic platform for the game, but Platinum arent known for their quality ports. It is a true shame that the port's issues will keep people from playing, and lower to mid tier PC's will struggle a good bit to run the game. Despite the technical flaws in the port, I truely belive this game deserves to be played.
The Game Itself scores a perfect 10/10, with the poor port dragging it down to an 8 or 9 depending on the power of your machine. But despite the poor port, NieR: Automata takes the cake as my absolute favorite game of all time. I highly recommend NieR, especially to those whom enjoy a rich story, beautifully crafted game world with atmosphere and tone that really makes you think. A roller coaster of many surprises twists and turns, definitely pick up NieR: Automata. If not on PC, then PS4

Still, the controller is not for everyone, in particular i can't see it being viable in any way over a fight stick, or even the ps4 controller for fighting games. Additionally, the controller really requires you to hold it a certain way, so that your pinkie and ring fingers rest on the grips. Even then, you can get thumb cramps if you don't relax your thumbs enough while playing. What's more the controller feels horrendously cheap, unsatisfying grip clicks, unintuitive button placement for ybxe ,and a horrible looking plastic shine on a portion of the controller.
I still exclusively use this controller for EVERYTHING besides working in eclipse, word, or any environment that requires a fair share of typing. Where the controller really shines is in it's software support, and just how in depth the customization is. I am a perfectionist, and this controller has no end to what it can do.
For example, take Guild Wars 2. While it's not everyone's kind of mmo, it's certainly designed for mouse and keyboard. After about 30 minutes of customizing keybindings, touch menus, button combos for macros, gyro control for certain actions, touch menu icons, and a bit of in game settings, the game was fully playable with the controller. What's even crazier is that it became enjoyable, and even more addicting using this controller! Suddenly this game felt super accessible because i didn't have to fiddle with number keys and f1-5 keys. Suddenly  0 - 9, and F1-F5 became accessible at any time while i was playing. I decided to get crazier and bind movement to the left touch pad, and readjusted some more options and was amazed at just how many inputs i could cram into this controller. From my experience there is only one thing that can rival the steam controller for guild wars 2 for me, and that is a keyboard and mouse WITH a number pad ( preferably up to 11 ). Even then, it's nowhere near as comfortable.
There are just so many things you can make this controller do. One trick i started using for games that had a sprint option was to have wasd (or joystick input, if supported by game ) bound to left touch pad, while the outer of the pad ( about halfway from the center, actually ) being bound to sprint.  Touch menus are amazing and essentially turn both touch pads into inputs for 12 buttons each EVEN IF you have left for movement and right for camera. My ONLY gripe about customization, is how useless the joystick is now. If valve had the option for a radial menu of up to 9 options appear  for every 15 or so degrees it would be perfect.
Is this controller better than a keyboard and mouse? The group consensus is no, not by a long shot. And i have to say i can't argue, if you're playing a game competitively kb + m is hard to beat. Especially when you factor in things like the logitech g600 and razer naga. However, i'd argue this not to be the case all the time, this thing can really surprise you if you're willing to give it some time. This controller might have been designed with the intent to make a lot of pc games couchable, but in the right hands it does so much more.

I'm pretty disappointed with the Steam Controller.
My initial thoughts when I unpacked the Steam Controller was that it felt very cheap and hollow. It feels bulky, yet it weights almost nothing, which gives it a weird weight-to-size ratio. I expected a more robust, heavier and overall higher quality product for €70, which it ended up costing me. The buttons gives very sharp and unsatisfying clicks, as if the insides consists of nothing but plastic cogs and bolts (imagine a controller for one of those very low budget RC helicopters or something). Felt like I was gonna break the whole thing when I first popped in the batteries.
So what about comfort? Honestly, it feels odd to hold it. Well at least with my hands. Maybe you'll get used to it after a while (I haven't), or perhaps it's my hands that are disfigured. The palm rests/grips point upward instead of down, opposed to the 360 controller for PC. It's probably designed that way so your thumbs can point down into the touchpads but to me it just feels like I'm standing on my hands on the edge of a skyscraper - pretty uncomfortable.
The button layout is OK, although the more I played with it the more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the two touchpads felt. I would've prefered a twin-stick setup with one touchpad. Some games just didn't work at all with the touchpads and it left me and my pals arguing about who would have to play with the Steam Controller. If you still persist on buying one - for the love of god, buy two so you can avoid that argument.
There are some positives though: you can switch between wired or wireless and it's highly customizable. Although some options feels very unnecessary, for instance the ability to change the brightness on the Steam button (which isn't that bright to begin with) or start-up and shutdown sounds (who cares? Just do the good ol' beep-boop). Can't really complain about it, since I'd rather have too many options than too few.
It's also perfect for "Big Picture Mode". Swapping through the different screens feels smooth and typing is much easier than with other controllers. It almost feels like it was made soley for navigating through Steam on Big Picture Mode. Oh... maybe THAT'S why it's called the Steam Controller? Because that's what I'm mainly going to use it for - to control Steam.
TL;DR: Wouldn't recommend it to anyone. The Xbox 360 controller for PC is still the best gamepad experience my hands has embraced. It's made for Big Screen Mode, basically.
