Disclaimer: these are only my first impressions of the game and not really my final thoughts.
Deus Ex: Human Revolution is a dense bomb that appears like a simple game with not much to offer to the player, but once you use it, you'll see that the explosion is that of a nuclear bomb. Essentially this game is a - mainly - story-driven game that mixes some story elements from the Crysis-series with Fallout 3/New Vegas.
It's a new era where the ethical questions of mechanical implants in humans are top discussions, naturally, this leads to protests.. sometimes to the extreme. You're Adam Jensen and you work for Sarif Industries which is the leading research company for these implants (augmentations, in-game), however, there's a terrorist attack by the anti-augmentation group and you almost die, however, augmentations to the rescue, you live! However, as you're sent off to an investigation to find out what/who was *really* going on behind this terrorist attack, you find out some things that were never meant to be found out. Either way, story so-far is fantastic and really interesting!
If you're the type of person who always prefers shooting and killing, well, you can do just that! You can also go stealthy through the entire game - marvelous. It does blend the two very well, and I find myself to prefer being stealthy because it's smoother and better implemented. Guns feel as if they're not really meant to be the primary choice of the player, and do feel somewhat dumbed-down, because aiming is a little difficult and the only real weapon with good accuracy is the standard pistol. Other than that, it does work quite well and it's different, so I won't complain. Ammo has to be bought and sold which adds some challenge to the game, so you can't really "run-and-shoot", you have to keep your strategies organised, which I definitely like, and the Fallout-aspects really shows off here.
Animations are buttery smooth and they really do a cool thing here. Instead of making the speech-animations (body animations) generic and stale, they have several to fit in with the situation and feelings and loop them which gives it all quite a good variety and more natural than you'd expect. Not to mention the stellar voice-acting. Voice acting is seriously top-notch. Doesn't get much better!
I really enjoy this game and feel as if more people HAVE TO own it, those who enjoy Fallout 3/New Vegas & Crysis 2, 3, in particular! I can't believe I've had it in my library for so long without giving it a glance.
9,4/10.

I thought this game was early access when it was gifted to me by a friend, I didn't realise it was a full release. I'd say in this state it's not a worthwhile purchase, it's essentially a less polished version of 'Lost Castle'. The combat is janky, the controls can be unpredictable and the game itself is buggy and appears to be prone to disconnecting frequently in co-op.
My biggest complaint is that we bought this for the co-op, but frankly it's not enjoyable with the friendly-fire the way it is currently. The game is a hack and slash, so the screen can sometimes become a bit of a cluster-♥♥♥♥ sometimes, which 90% of the time lead to either my friend or me being bashed into the air over and over which then gets us both killed. Seriously, the friendly-fire-but-not-quite (you can hit each other with literally anything you do, spells, scrolls, attacks, but none of it does any damage, just knocks the other player around) is incredibly frustrating, and is the reason we stopped playing this game. I'm going to be trying to get a steam gift refund for my friend who gifted it to me. I might check on this game again in 6 months, but if you're considering getting it I'd advise getting Lost Castle instead, it's the exact same game but with a much better design.
Don't get me wrong, I don't mind frustrating games. I loved the Dark Souls series, and I don't mind difficult and grindy rogue-likes. This game isn't frustrating because it's challenging, or because the enemies are too hard, or anything like that. It's frustrating as a result of broken mechanics and poor design choices.
Final thoughts;
I cannot recommend this game. It feels like a sloppy rip-off of Lost Castle, and is extremely frustrating (but not in the good way).

- Combat is fairly entertaining due to satisfying feedback on hitting enemies. Weak attacks still visibly stun enemies for a short moment. Stronger attacks throw them around forcefully, rendering them prone and defenseless to getting picked from the ground and thrown again. Single normal-sized foes can be defeated easily, but with time.
- Difficulty can be challenging, due to limit of lives and permadeath. A higher challenge level is probably the more popular option, with this type of game?!
- Replayability through randomization of levels, enemies and loot. New playable characters to unlock.
- Loot is very original and varied. Some of the weapons and armors have amazingly unusual traits. E.g. I found an armor that exploded on hit, not just once but repeatedly, whenever a foe landed a blow on me. The armor also granted me immunity to explosions.
- Very enjoyable when you can find a friend, who's addicted to progressing further in the maps, to play coop with.
Yet, here are the reasons why I'll probably never play it again:
- The basic combat you start out with (loot might change that?) is too limited in engaging variety, although the few moves available are well animated and impressive to perform/watch.
There are 2 special moves that can be performed from a normal attack combo, a dash attack performed through charging a button press and a kick that is context sensitive and only triggers if you press attack while standing in a precise proximity to the foe (in other words, you cannot rely on it). All of these can be comboed in flashy ways, but it only rarely feels rewarding. There are usually only small amounts of enemies on screen and many (if not all) can move fairly swiftly. The difficulty of killing them lies in their big amounts of hitpoints and your weak beginning weapon (which you return to, after every permadeath).
Performing the same small amount of moves on the same enemies, over and over, had me tired of it after 15 minutes.
The beat 'em ups that I enjoyed (e.g. "Warriors of Fate") had more combat variety. And I'd rather need a step up from that, in 2017.
- The loot is exciting...but you can never keep it! You die, it's gone.
Discovering all of the items that are available can be enjoyable with a friend, I guess. But...
- The game is rather boring when you cannot find entertaining company for cooperative play.
Would I recommend the game? Yes, to fans of beat 'em ups without much combat variety.
Do I like the game, though? No.

I had very high expectations going into this game. +Satisfying combat
+Gorgeous visuals

Cons:
-World is too large with too little to do and little reward for exploration
-There aren't many different areas, meaning you'll be visiting the same locations and travelling between them over and over

-Sidequests are tedious and usually resort to "go from point A to point B and talk to this person then go back to point A" or "go to this area and farm materials then come back to me"; I enjoyed the game much more once I started ignoring the sidequests

TL;DR Enjoyable game but overhyped. Get it on sale, preferably on PS4 to avoid PC porting issues.

I purchased this a while back, in order to introduce me to the BlazBlue franchise that I've heard about for a while now, and let me tell you, this game surpassed my expectations.
This game is grand. The visuals are spectaclarly detailed. The voice acting is, overall, wonderful, with only a couple of flat performances. There isn't much wrong in this game, other than a few nit-picky things that are purely my opinion, but I'm pretty sure that someone out there agrees with me. I mean, it isn't something that's going to distract you too much, as the characters with the flat acting only appear once or twice in the story mode, and there are far from important to the plot (they aren't even named so I have no clue why I'm complaining - _ -'), but it's just a little thing I noticed. Another thing is how many cliff-hangers there are in the story. I know, I know, that's like saying that I don't want a sequel, and that I don't like the mystery, which I do; but still, they could at least wrap up a few things. Despite my nit-picks, BlazBlue: Calamity Trigger is one awesome game. Take it from a new fan who's downloading the sequel as he types; if you haven't played this game, you really should.

I was never much into fighting games...
Until I played this one.
Blazblue: Calamity Trigger is one of the best fighting games I've ever played (and I've played some in all my gaming years). Most games in this style just demand that the player keep pressing buttons to win, or keep spaming the same movements over and over again. This is not the case here. The learning curve of Calamity Trigger is not easy, but it's certainly rewarding.
You have 12 characters to play from, and to some, this may be a small amount to play with. But the thing here is that you don't have two characters who have a similar style. Everyone has different fighting mechanics, and certainly, one of them will become your favorite:
You have Ragna the Bloodedge, who fights with both his giant sword, and using his fists and kicks, and is able to drain life from his opponent when he uses his Azure Grimmoire. There is Jin Kisaragi, who have a sword similar to a katana, and has ice powers. There is Noel Vermillion, who uses two giant pistols. There is Rachel Alucard, who is similar to a lady doll from the noble parts of society, who uses his shapeshifting cat and his sidekick to move graceously in the battlefield. Use her special movement (Those are called Distortion Drive in this game) early in the battle, and you will probably miss, but try to spread Lighting Rods and then using the Distortion, and all of them will get energized by the movement. Some of the characters even use their Heat Gauge (Used to make Distortion Drives) differently from other characters, and this variety of gameplay is one of the things that makes this franchise killer, not mentioning all the counter movements, throws, defensive maneuvers and ways to even use your Heat Gauge to extend combos.
The story is another major point of this game. You have 10 character's story mode to complete. Two of them are not included. In each campaign, you have different routes in the story based on some dialog choices, and even losing specific battles will not result in Game Over, rather opening another path to go on. Even the way you finish your battles may alter the route. Every character's story mode has a percentage of completion, and to get 100%, you will need to see every possible outcome. This way, you will be able to reach the true ending of that character's campaign...but does that mean the other ones are alternative endings? Check to story and draw your own conclusions.
In Calamity Trigger, you basically have the Story, Versus, Score Attack and Arcade modes. In the Arcade, you will choose one character to defeat 10 others, and in specific encounters, you will even have a dialog. It's a simple game mode, but not short of surprises. Some interesting rewards await those who complete it.
The game is completely dubbed, both in japanese and english, and has subtitles as well. I didn't play in English, but the Japanese one is awesome, as expected.
The only let-down is that it has no online mode, but trust me, you will spend dozens of hours in this game if you want to take the most of it.
Finally, it has one of the most amazing soundtracks I've ever heard. It's a mix of classical music and heavy metal, and if you're into that style of music, you will be delighted. Best of all, you will get the full digital OST in MP3 buying this.
That said, Blazblue: Calamity Trigger is recommended both to the ones who enjoy an awesome fighting game, and to those you're just getting started in that genre. Trust me, you will not be disappointed.

An overpriced parts exploder, this alleged game is more of an interactive firearms reference than it is something someone might be found actually playing with rather than reviewing  for extended periods of time. If one were to take this game at a full $50 dollar value for the current set of guns and whatever future shooty-bangs may be made available, you'll be quite at odds with trying to identify what it is your actually paying for. Am I buying a pop-up book minus the quality narrative contained within a book that satisfactorily describes it's subject or am I buying something I expect to toy with on an occasional basis? The problem I see with this game right now is that it couldn't lend itself to both purpose without hurting the interests (and attention) of the user who is trying to justify his or her purchase.
World of Guns visualizes and explains the workings of firearms by taking the user through the anatomy of his or her gun of choice. On the basis of the starting weapon alone, the AK-47, we're walked through a very accurate representation of the process of field stripping the weapon right up to the extent of fully disassembling the gun and restoring it to its original state. Afterwards we are treated to an interactive review of how the gun fires; allowing us the option of slowing down time and reviewing the entire cycling action of the weapon through cut-away views and x-rays that makes the whole thing a rather interesting and informative affair. It does this, however, through a point and click interface that's just as mechanical as the subject it covers.
This game has more potential to be a successful interactive firearms encyclopedia with the help of more in depth commentary on the guns themselves than woefully tacked on shooting ranges and field stripping competitions of who gets to be the fastest clicker. The shooting range component of the game is a terrible, awkward experience and, taken with the notion that this game tries to do guns accurately, it's dismaying to think about how something like Receiver is doing a better job of portraying the "feel" of a gun than this game is at that level.
At full price, this three dimensional parts exploder could be justified by those who seek to learn more and work on the mechanics of the guns that they either have, want to have, or already have. There isn't enough "game" in this alleged game for it to be, by any means, considered fun. The whole idea behind World of Guns seem like it exists to inform and explore while what game there is to be had with it is either forced or altogether unappealing.
At no price, this game can attract the person wanting to see how guns work but will subsequently turn them away what with how it tries to convince itself and the user that it is indeed a game that requires the him or her to level up. There isn't a game to be had here and there definitely isn't a reason to keep coming back to a mechanical point and click job to unlock the next thing.
At a starter price there is hardly any value to be had when given the prospect of having to inevitably come back to the same point and click job again and again and be given the option to pay for more to either straight up unlock the next gun or gain experience faster.
While World of Guns is advertised as a game (or sim for that matter) it is more worth it's price had it been appropriately designed and made to be as a well polished interactive virtual armory minus the leveling up and lamentable micro transactions. As it stands it does the part of being an expensive parts exploder very well, but not much else.

Sure, the game does not run very smoothly, and you need to make an .ini file configuration to unlock the framerate, however the game itself is definitely worth the time, of someone who loves the zombie genre/culture in general. In hindsight, if the game didn't have the optimization and performance that it did have during launch, I'm pretty certain that this game would be rated FAR higher, than it is right now.
Game is about roaming inside a city sandbox filled with zombies (and I really mean FILLED). Building weapons and vehicles of carnage and destruction to eviscerate, shred, slice and bludgeon the zombies to a pulp. If you enjoy violent and gory video games, this will most definitely tickle your fancy. Story is a mixed bag, but has some great cameos, that surprise you, if you were playing the previous games at some point, and still remember some of the characters. Psychopath enemies are just as crazy (maybe even more so in this game) as they were in all of the Dead Rising games, and some of them were downright disturbing. The inital cover and the "look" of the game might be deceiving at first, implying that it's a "realistic" zombie survival game, but I'm really glad that it isn't.
- An insanely expansive selection of different weapons, combos, super combos, firearms, explosives... ET CETERA. If at any point of your life have you wondered what would be like shooting zombies with a high-powered dil...ahem "massager" cannon - this game might answer your question.
- No escort missions. They were extremely repetative, but necessary for proper completion, in previous games. Here the survivors can use any weapons you give them, and the AI is actually pretty good, since they will follow your lead ANYWHERE and even up obsticles, jumping to buildings.
- A generous time limit. If you're a bit salty over getting a whole week, in-game time, to complete the game, consider starting the game immediately on "Nightmare mode", since from my personal experience, I can tell that it was made for more experienced Dead Rising players. You have less time, and it starts counting down the second you get control of your character in the tutorial. You get 5 days, not 7.
- Proper learning curve. You no longer feel limited by the controls of the game, which previous games had. You have additional buttons for melee attacks and you can finally SPRINT SPRINT SPRINT. Who knew that a zombie game with a time-sensitive direction would benefit from a sprinting mechanic?
- Comfortable controls (played with a gamepad)
- Decent performance on an AMD GPU (R9 280X). Played the game on "High", 1080p with SMAA, and had no real issues. Yes the game sometimes dipped to high 30's, but that wasn't frequent. Most of the time, game stayed at high 40, low 50's and 60fps, when I was running is less crowded areas.
- Almost no loading screens. Dead Rising 2 had an abyssmal amount of loading screens and a lot of areas with loading screens. However, this time around there are very few load screens, and most of them occur when switching from cutscenes into gameplay. World is seamless, across all 4 "islands".
- Progression feels generic. More health, faster combination, more damage. etc.
- Not very many useful combo weapons. A good chunk of them you'll probably craft once, and never use again.
- Controls aren't fluid enough, but it's still a huge improvement over the older games.
- Story is B movie quality at best, but if you enjoy the cheesy popcorn, it's probably one of the best in the zombie genre.
- You can't combine weapons without blueprints. This is probably the biggest issue with the current combo system, since it discourages personal experimentation, while Dead Rising 2 encouraged it. You know for a fact that those components will mix, but you can't without a blueprint.
- Overall an easy experience. Bosses are not challenging, because the combo weapons (especially the Elemental Staff) just melt the bosses away like they're boogers under a water faucet. Solving the control and ease of use issues made the game too accessible for older players of the series.
- You are never required to combine weapons again, since you can cherry pick them out of the "Safe Zone" lockers. Sure, you can't just pick 10 Elemental Staffs, but you can pick 2, which still sort of makes the combo mechanic redundant during the later stages of the game, since you can just pick up a freshly made weapon, without any crafting.
- Not enough vehicle combos. There's only 10 of them, and some of them don't feel too much different from the other.
- Bad VSYNC. If you remove the framerate cap, whenever the game goes down by at LEAST two or three frames, it instantly locks it to 30fps. Unless you have a really poweful setup, that will NEVER dip your framerate, consider disabling in-game VSYNC, and using an alternative way to remove screen tearing.
- Co-op, since I still haven't properly played it. People to my knowledge can HARM your survivors, but you can also instantly kick them, so there's no real problem here. VOIP seems to be working fine, with what little experience I had with it.
- DLC, aside from the extra outfits, vehicles, weapons you get. Outfits are sort of disappointing, but some of the weapons   are really kick♥♥♥♥♥
Dead Rising 3 is a good game. Shocker, huh? It does have performance issues and framerate locks, but there are ways around it. The hate is definitely deserved for the quality the game had during the launch, and it deserves the hit in reputation that it received, however I see no reason to ignore a fun game like this. It can be played with a friend or solo, it has lots of bloodshed, it's not frustratingly difficult (which made some people turn away from Dead Rising in the past) and it also manages to create an interesting world to wreck some zombies in. Cannot recommend this game enough, if you enjoy the zombie genre.
Congratulations to the Devs, excellent work!

shooter made by men with long, curly hair and mustaches that were flecked with
recently inhaled gamer food. It was from Georgia, crafted in tiny studios and
played by first-call QA testers who could fall into a smooth grave at will. The
game was fast and spacious and kissed by soul and lite-quake, but it
steered away from corridor sized grit. Though the people making the game lived decadent
lives and considered themselves post-90s rebels of a kind, their aesthetic fit
perfectly on adult contemporary Steam Sale. It's been murdering the souls of competitive gamers in the TeamSpeak channel ever since.

Ordered the Controller last month as a treat to myself.  ( See Unboxing vid here -
)
Now that I've had a few weeks to mess about with the controller, I feel as though I can give a better opinion.
Overall. I love it. Why?
- The keys are rebindable in game, so it's pretty damned customisable from the get go.
- There's a good community of alteratives for a good majority of games.
- To me, it feels very well constructed
- Tactile feedback that can be adjusted, so you can have none to full on
- Wired or Wireless, and the wireless is 2 AA batteries. I bought 4 AA USB rechargables purely for the controller! 2 in use, 2 on charge..
- Touch pads are brilliant! I love the fact you can use it as a virtual mouse/roller ball when you're not gaming.
- Additional buttons! You have the usual 4 shoulde buttons, and there's 2 more on the grip.
- Everything has a nice 'click' and feel
- Everything is confirgurable through Big Picture mode
- Configurable tuning off and on sounds!
I will say it does take some getting used to. Especially with the right touch pad. But that's all part of the fun!  =D
There's some games that don't work that well with the controller, and for me, at least, are best played with Keyboard & Mouse (Mainly FPS shooter games).
I would still stongly suggest though, if you have available funds , get one!!

Great controller, definitely prefer it now over the Xbox controller. Took a day or so to get used to the button and joystick positions, and I'm only used to the back paddles on certain games, but it is a really nice controller once you get used to it. The haptic feedback is a nice touch to the touchpads, and can also be used as rumble/vibration simulation (as an experiemental feature)
FPS games are obviously difficult to play with, just like with any controller. I do enjoy Racing/Driving games (Rocket League, GRID 2, and driving in GTAV) using this controller, as well as games such as The Binding of Issac. Cities: Skylines isn't too bad either, though I still prefer a mouse and keyboard (that's just personal preferance, however).
The hand grips are a bit big, and it would be nice if they were a tad bit smaller, and some games only work with it if the game was launched using Big Picture (Rocket League and GTAV come to mind). Valve has made a temporary fix for this by giving users the option to launch a game in Big Picture whenever the controller is turned on, but the Big Picture overlay is a bit laggy, and doesn't have certain features such as an FPS counter. The controller buttons/touchpad settings also can only be configured through the Big Picture overlay.
Overall, it's a great product, but I kinda wish Valve would fix the software side of the controller, and the hand-grips being big is a bit of a bummer, but that still doesn't change the fact that it is still a great controller!

Firstly, I have to get the fact you won't want this if you don't enjoy messing around with configurations out of the way. Otherwise, the sheer volume of possibilities for creative sets of controls, sometimes easier to use than kbm in addition to the comfort of a controller.
I have to admit, my first few hours I was pretty underwhelmed. Initially I made the purchase because I play a LOT of turn based games ( especially XCom and Endless legend ) and wanted to play them laying back instead of hunched over a desk. It served tha purpose but took some getting used to. I didn't know if I'd get much other use of it, and that was fine.
I decided to try a bunch of other games just to give it a fair chance. Some games it was ok, since for whatever reason they didn't include controller support. Just took some configuration. Slowly as I went through the sheer volume of options I realized there's a lot more potential than I thought. This was most apparent with Kerbal Space Program which has a truely amazing setup ( I prefer it over kbm now! ) that feels great after figuring it all out. Especially since it automaically changes control scheme based on what it is you're doing. Between this and the ability to map ways to swap to a new mapping, it became clear tha there's more to this device.
An amazing feature is the feedback. Adjustable and it really helps you literally feel out the controls/responses. Especially with the tracking ball simulation and joystick settings.
I'll still probably use my elite controller for anything that supports it, but I'll get a lot more use out of this than I first thought. I look forward to being creative about creating intuitive ways to play games with complex controls from the comfort of my couch.

First off, I don't really play any singleplayer First Person Shooter stuff other than the two CoD campaigns I played. But DOOM really surprised me. If you don't get this game, you're practically committing a crime.

You can upgrade a bunch of various things about your character.

Overall, the game is great and extremely fun. Totally recommended.

I really wanted to love this, I really effin' love brawlers and this looked so good. I tried to enjoy it, I really did, but it's just not a good brawler. Movement feels really clunky, attacking stops you dead, something's off about the horizontal planes or your attack's hitbox so enemies can be just slightly above you and your sword swings will completely miss, and combat's basically mashing a single attack button over and over. Granted, you can also press up, down and either left or right to do a directional attack, but it's not implemented well and is very awkward to perform as you have to be attacking your enemy before you can do it.
It's not all bad; there's a huge variety of weapons, items, spells and unlockables, and they're generally really well thought out. It's obvious a lot of work went into the RPG aspects of the game, and they work brilliantly because I'd constantly be weighing up whether a new spell was worth dropping an old one, or whether a potion should be drunk now or would the side effects screw me over, so in that regard the game's great. It's just a shame the movement and the combat just didn't seem to "click" for me, because I'd be more willing to retry that awful Pit and Pendulum boss if it handled better.

Verdict: Nier Automata is one of the awesome AAA game of 2017.

It's rare that a developer goes from make a adult game about crime with very adult themes. To making a game about a high school kid who moves to a school for child delinquents and socially challenged kids, but in a lot of ways Bully is like a GTA. For example Bully is a giant open world with stuff to collect, bike races to do, arcade games to play, and much more to just kind of find.The mission structure is very similar to GTA, you do a bunch of work for one of the factions;like the jocks or the nerds, and the more the more you do work for one faction it can effect your standing with others. Which in turn can effect the way some of the people treat you at school. The combat is very similar but instead of machine guns and rocket launches. Your playing with slingshots and stink bombs. There are also a lot of things that are different about Bully that really makes it feel like your in high school it feel very structured, but that's not a bad thing at all. Like you have classes two times a day everyday until you pass the highest level of that class, and of you don't go the prefects or any adult of authority. All the classes have there own perks like one of the classes shows you where all the collectibles, and unlike the protagonists in GTA jimmy is 15 and needs his sleep so if your out past 2 you just pass out on the spot which can make some night missions feel a little too time restrictive.
The story starts you out in a car ride with you and your mom and what seems to be your new stepdad. They then drop you off in the front of Bullyworth academy where you meet the principle and some of the teacher, but the fun starts to come in when you go to your dorm room and meet your new friend Gary, who is a sociopath, i don't know how else to put it.You soon start to become manipulated by him, and you two soon go your separate ways and you start to see less and less of him. You then start to do work for the other factions of the school. Playing Bully it kind of puts you back and makes you think about your time in high school, I know the archetypes aren't as plain and simple as they are in Bully but it does a great job of boiling a lot of the high school experience down to a 20 hour game.
Then there are a few technical issues with bully I didn't really have too many other then the game crash on me a couple of times, and that just sucks after that happened for the first time a started saving much more frequently. I can't really say definitely how the game will turn out for you, but it didn't seem to bad. From my experience with it. Over all the game is well made but parts of it just seem kind of repetitive and broken;overall though I think it's a great game.

I have owned two racing games that have filled my heart with love, joy, thrills and spills - Grand Prix 2 and Grand Prix 4.  Now, finally, after years of searching, I own a third. Hands down the best racing game I have played in well over a decade.
The single seater racing is a thrill straight off the bat, add some mods and basically you have an updated version of Crammonds masterpiece back in your library. Perfectly balanced for someone like me who's not a total hardcore sim racing nut, but understands the parameters of racing and likes to be rightly and fairly punished by a physics model when they get it wrong, yet retain the ability to tune and increase the difficulty as I learn more. In short cars that behave like cars, always and honestly - no rubber banding here. There have been no other games for years where within a matter of hours I could balance the game perfectly for both my skills and deficiencies (oh that sense of being on the limit), so that I could go bumper to bumper with the AI  for three laps working out my plan of attack, waiting for them to twitch with the torque or knowing when my brakes and tyres were right in the zone and it was now or never - genius racing.
Welcome back my beautifully modded 1996 F1 season, welcome back Johnny Herbert and Luca Badoer.  Welcome back cars that crack in two and loose wheels spinning across the track. Welcome back first corner mayhem and last lap fights with man and machinery. They say that motor racing is about split seconds - this game makes me regret every second, minute and hour I've spent in Codemasters hell looking, and hoping to find this. I'm so glad I finally found you, and my heartfelt thanks to the development team. A racing game that makes me smile again.

Automobilista is a must have for any sim racing enthusiast. Seriously. Get it now. Doesn't matter if it's on sale or not, this game is easily worth full asking price. Make sure to get the DLC season pass as well - it's amazing.
Consider getting the game straight from Reiza as AMS + Full Season Pass gains you access to Reiza 51. I was not aware of it and bought it on Steam. Reiza has sales as well if that's important to you, just check their forums from time to time.
Casual gamers that are just getting their feet wet in simracing may be better off just getting the game straight from Steam, so in a rare case they don't like the game they can request a refund.
Back to the sim.
AMS calls itself motorsports simulator and that's what it is. Since it's all race cars you won't find road cars in the official content, but that's what the mods are for.
Speaking of mods, there is a track pack by Patrick Giranthon (google it) that looks like official content - it's pretty much a must have. The game has some well know tracks such as Imola, Adelaide, Hockenheim, Montreal, Suzuka etc. but some famous tracks are missing (licensing maybe?) and the track pack from Patrick rounds up the sim quite nicely.
This is what every sim racer cares about. Simply put - I find it superb. Others agree. Physics guru Niels Heusinkveld is part of the Reiza team. Do I need to say more?
Automobilista has huge range of cars - open wheelers, go karts, tin tops, dirt, even trucks, and all are outstanding to drive. Whether you are a fan of Formula 1 (this is probably THE SIM for Formula 1 enthusists as it covers F1 cars from vintage '67 models all the way to the modern bolids) or just want to fool around in FWD Honda Civic you will find something for yourself.
The quality of all the official cars is excellent.
Another important aspect, often overlooked is how devs respond to suggestions/complaints/. Reiza is very good listenig to their userbase and active/helpful on the forums.
I've seen some complaints (mostly on youtube from folks that don't even own the game) that graphics could be better and maybe it's true if one compares it to Project Cars, but by all means it's not bad. It doesn't bother me at all, I don't find it lacking. Great physics and sublime force feedback more than make up for it. Someone said "if graphics bothers you then you drive too slow" and I agree ;-)
We have to remember that AMS is based on rFactor engine, but Reiza took it to another level.
Finally, Reiza won't nickel and dime you with DLC. In fact they add content for free. If you get season pass all future content will be available to you for no additional price.
They just added Metalmoro AJR to the base game. BASE GAME. That car is so good that the game is worth getting just for Metalmoro series alone, and they added it for FREE. This is absolutely crazy.
Check Metalmoro AJR on youtube. Amazing, amazing cars. Brasilian equivalent of LMP2.
No game is perfect and AMS is no exception.
There is occasional error loading textures. Quick integrity check always solves it, but it's a nuisance reminiscent of old rFactor.
To sum up:

-physics
-FFB
-perfected content - all cars are refined to the highest level
-good AI for offline racing
-great support
-all future DLC included in price of Season Pass
-great modding community
-hot lapping to compare oneself to other drivers if you don't have time to play online
-occasional stuttering on some computers - only pre v1.4.9
-occasional crashes while loading new tracks, corrupted files (Steam integrity check fixes it)
-I didn't test it as I have no time to play online, but people complain it's hard to find a game unless you are part of a league. That is the problem with all the sims however, maybe except iRacing

Automobilista unquestionably is among one of best racing simulators ever created. Automobilista is a top-tier game that has everything a true racing sim should have. Man, im surprised I didn't write a review for Paladins earlier.
I went on a hiatus for a few months, leaving shortly after Lux was added. I thought I enjoyed my time very much, and as sure to return eventually when there's a lot more content to explore. Sadly, now it comes to possibly one of the most backstabbing patches I've seen in gaming. The characters were very enjoyable, and the amount of customization you had over champions made it a very possible competitor to Overwatch, as many people enjoy having loadouts to play with their own personal touch.
Previously, the system already had issues with a new player experience, but it was somewhat bearable because everyone was on a largely level playing field, and it didn't take too long to get most cards for most champions, and after awhile you would get several champs under your belt where you could use anything you wanted.
However, the new system is literally Star Wars BattleFront II, but worse. While you do start with every card, all cards will be at a pathetically low level, and the only way to improve them is to grind. grind. grind. and hope rng favors you extremely heavily, as you need (as of PTS Update #5) about 50 of any common card to reach its maximum level. Legendaries, being far rarer, still require 10 duplicates of the same legendary to reach the same level. This means that, unless you dedicate actual months to the game, you will perpetually be at a lower level playing field compared to other players, especially those who pay to get ahead. To even get ahead through this method, it is balanced around requiring hundreds of dollars just to get any single champion to a decent level, if you are lucky enough to get cards for them.
Even worse is that they are implementing a gold per day cap, so you are even punished for investing time into the game to try to catch up
Not only that, but the very same update removes almost all decision making from your loadouts, and even hinders your ability to pick certain champions, as theres little to no reason to play a champion when you don't have any decent cards for them.
I really, really wish I could spread the same fun I had with Paladins when I first played it, but I just cant speak kindly about the game when OB64 arrives this Wednesday (12/13/17). It just isn't worth it. Maybe someday the game will return, but until then, I just cant recommend this game.

I've played the original BlazBlue on Xbox (Arcade) and I love it that they did a remake on that game (or more like a PC port). My expections were pretty high and I didn't get dissapointed!
But first thing first:
-> Spoiler warning for the story! If you haven't played the "real ending",skip to the next arrow!
-The Story:
There isn't really much of a story... it's a tournament fighter like Street Fighter,what do you expect? Oh well,here's the Story: Ragna and his brother Jin were normal boys who lived in a church/an orphanage with nuns. One day the building started to burn and Ragna quickly noticed it (He was in the Woods BTW). As he retuned,Jin was standing there,telling him that he's the reason this happened. At first he didn't understand,but then it was too late. Jin cut off Ragna's arm. Now we're skipping ahead at least 10 years. Ragna's grown up and wants to get revenge for his arm and the nuns Jin had killed. On his way to Jin he met some people and most of em' wanted his "Azure Grimoire", wich is giving him Demon like powers. At the NOL HQ,the meets Jin to finally settle the score, but they were interrupted when a gate opened,that connected the "Real World" to the "Under World". There he met V-13,a robot like girl who says that she's his sister. In the final cutscene, Rachel Alucard uses a spell with wich she's trying to close the gate. Of course, it didn't work
-> Spoiler free Arrow right here!
And thats the whole story! Of course, it's incomplete. It's getting more complete in the 2nd game,Continuum Shift,wich will be soon available on Steam. Overall the story is Ok.
-The Characters:
This is an interessting thing to talk about. You have 11 playable characters. Those would be "Ragna the Bloodedge","Bang Shishigami","Jin Kisaragi","Noel Vermillion","Carl Clover","Rachel Alurad","Taokaka","Litchi Faye-Ling","Arakune","V-13" and "Hakumen",Each with differen attack speeds and Distortion Finishes. And that's really a shame. Don't get me wrong,I like the characters, but in what minds did they think to leave out Hazama??? He is one of,if THE, coolest characters in this entire game! But he's only an NPC... at least he's playable in Continuum Shift.
-The Gamemodes:
That's a simple one. There are only some modes. Story,Arcade and Online. There are the most important ones and the only ones.
-The Gameplay:
This game plays as you would expect it to. There's a light,medium and heavy attack button,Special attack buttons, Combos for Distortion Finishes (ect.). If you've ever played any fighting game like Street Fighter or Tekken,you know how to play BlazBlue!
There's nothing more to say to this I guess... Moving on!
-The Graphic:
Oh my god, the graphic... It's so beautiful. All characters look like they belong in an Anime, the intro cutscene and some other cutscenes are drawn (Animestyle) and the backgrounds are not just "there", they feel alive because something's allways happening! If you're a fan of Anime,you're gonna like the visuals of this game,bright and shiny on one side, dark and kinda scary on the other. A perfect mix!
-The Music:
I've saved the best for last!
THIS says everything I need to say. The music a AWSOME! It's Powerfull,Epic and most importantly remindable. If I think about BlazBlue, the song that always comes to my mind would be Taokakas theme. It's so happy and *Derp* at the same time...It's perfect for Taokaka.
All in all,this game ROCKS! You should DEFINATLY,DEFINATLY buy this game! C'mon! Buy it allready! Go ahead!
My final Score for this game is 10/10 Points. It's simply a masterpiece.

Paris in the Autumn...
Of all the references, the George Stobbart one was the best and this is reason enough to recommend the game! :D
All joking aside, I really can't understand the negative thoughts regarding the subject matter of the game. It has a pretty standard Orwellian aesthetic, but acts as a satyre on current affairs: Mainly the finanancial crisis and increasingly harsh copyright laws, with nods to the refugee crisis, the ever increasing wealth divide, the importance of Art and the power of money.
From the credits, I gather the developer team is based in Spain and as such has first hand knowledge of all these themes. As a (southern) European myself, I can see where the inspiration comes from, and in no way I find it "too left", or "too out there".
On the other hand, I have some issues with the technical aspects of the game. The controls are better suited for a touch screen (it is a mobile port after all), and the (slow) walking back and forth was a tad annoying. But that's it mostly! The game is short, so just sit back and enjoy the story!
Oh, and Mme Merkel makes an appeareance too! :D

Great Fusion is a great little point-and-click adventure game that was initially released on Android and iOS back in 2014. It is now available on the PC - as usual the adaptation has slightly better graphics but some gameplay elements and the main menu easily give it away (i.e. you can clearly see it was initially meant for smartphones).
+++ Great hand-drawn graphics! It really reminds you of the old Lucasart's games that came out in the '90s.
+++ Similarly to those classic gems this one also uses humour as part of its story-telling. I especially liked the many references to films, music, celebritites, politicians and - naturally - to those classic games.
--- While the game has excellent soundtrack it misses the voice-acting. I'm not sure it would have greatly increased the file size considering it is not that long. Afterl all, current smartphones have quite the memory capacity these days. Or they could have just done the voiceover for this particular version. Remember Day of The Tentacle had 2 versions (one with and another without a dub)?
--- The smartphone effect: the inventory is opened by finding the button on the left side and moving the cursor (while the button is pressed) from left to right. Surely the press of a button would have sufficed.
Recommended purchase for adventure game fans; just bear in mind that it is relatively short due to it being an adaptation of a smartphone app.

Remember ye olden days when you played games like Streets of Rage or Double Dragon? Rampage Knights is a beat 'em up game where you travel along slashing and bashing enemies and crushing them beneath your feet. Much like the aforementioned games, this is also a cooperative game. You can play it with friends online or with local shared/split screen.
Along with the beat 'em up gameplay, it also has rogue-like elements to it. You go along through randomly generated areas and rooms, fighting against an array of enemies or having to avoid a fair many hazards. You can also gather items or spells along with equipping gear you might find to help you along the way. Along with these though, there are also diseases and curses which can hinder and harm you in different ways.
The game is likely best played in multiplayer with a friend. You won't find any friendly fire happening (at least at Normal difficulty) so you won't have any issues in that department, but some curses can effect both you and your friend as you go along. Watch out though if your friend throws an explosive - or watch out for your friends when you throw them.
Considering the strengths of the game, I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for its single player - but if you have a friend you are looking to play with, then a recommend picking it up the 2-pack on offer and playing it with them.

This game is what all FPS games should strive to be - realistic, but fun, with an emphasis on cooperative team play. The graphics may not be the best at this point, but this hardly detracts from the vivid environments, achieved through cunning use of textures (Dirt, dirt everywhere - war really is crap) and constant background noise of whistling bullets and artillery. Vehicular combat is expertly portrayed, with a proper crew being a must for effective employment and a balanced, but powerful presence. Infantry combat truly shines however, the details everywhere - overheating MG barrels, an ammunition feeder and a squad leader with communication equipment, interesting cover and ironsights mechanics as well as stamina and modular health system all contribute to a sense of accomplishment with every fragged opponent. For people who appreciate a team based conflict simulation, there are no Rambo's here; this is a game where "credit to team" really shines.

I like this a lot more than I thought I would, while I don't consider it a full replacement for either keyboard+mouse or pure console controller like xbox 360, it has many great advantages and depending on the game can perform better than either.
Depending on the game you can get the best of both worlds between kb/m and controller, the right thumbpad allows you to look around much more accurately and quickly in 3D games than a right thumbstick would allow you especially because of their deadzones and analog pressure features(which often has me turning faster and further than I need to) while maintaining the gamepad benefits of buttons, bumpers, triggers and left thumbstick, as well as a left thumbpad that can emulate Dpad.
At this point I've found very advantageous uses for it with certain games, but with some games like pure fighters etc, very console/gamepad focused games, I still prefer an xbox 360 controller. Similarly with very intensive simulation type PC games where a hundred buttons under your face actually contributes to the realism and ease of control, the steam controller is also not a replacement.
I find it an excellent couchmate for traditionally kb/m casual simulation games like city builders and 4x. Anything that's a lot of thinking and taking your time and pointing and clicking? This is a brilliant replacement for the office chair IMHO.

The more I drive it, the more I like it! No fancy graphics here, let's quickly put this aside: it is not meant for crazy screenshots or vids. But a great racing atmosphere, I find it really immersive once I'm in the cockpit. There is a large line up of different cars: lots of formulas (from 1975 to current ones), small fwd (Mini, Touring cars), rwd (old Opala or modern V8 Supercars and stock cars), awd (spec series Lancers or rallycross), all with distinct driving characteristics! The driving pleasure is huge each time but never the same. Track selection is large too: initially Brazil and South America orientated, there is now a large selection from all around the world, with the addition of old versions from the 60s and 70s (before the safety regulations...). What I like is to have complete series, with all cars and tracks from the calendar, and to run complete championships. There is not a career mode, but you can freely choose your chanllenges, and create your own career. Ais are great, they have been hugelly improved lately and provide nice battles! This game made me discover online too, a first for me; never tried public servers but found a nice club with people sharing the same passion:  it is a blast! So AMS is not reduced to hotlapping, even if it is possible too, with leader boards so you can compare your times. It is also nice to support a small developer: Reiza is a pretty small team, mostly a group of passionate people that create the sim they  dreamed of... and I'm lucky to share their dream! This game did improve a lot since its release, and is really a great package now.

Absolutely fantastic. The plot of this game is extraordinary. As a writer, I found myself thoroughly enthralled at the building conspiracy within this game. The Director's Cut offers a much better experience than the original release, which I have on console. The combat is fluid and extremely versatile. There are always alternatives to every given situation. If the player wants, he/she can pilot Adam Jensen through the whole game without killing, or even incapaciting, a single person (excluding the three boss fights).   I highly reccommend buying this game, and lose yourself in the rich storytelling that Square Enix delivers in Deus Ex: Human Revolution.
And remember..."Everybody Lies."

*Note I have over 80 hours logged on the normal Deus Ex: Human Revolution.
Deus Ex: Human Revolution is a phenomenal game.  Human Revolution takes place in 2027 and is a prequel to the original Deus Ex.  Playing the original is not required at all to understand the story, but I do suggest playing it simply because its a great game.  The story of Deus Ex: Human Revolution tackles the subject of Transhumanism in a way that really makes you think.  The subject matter is complex and is an issue that we will likely face in the not to distant future.  The gameplay is really solid but there is a lot of room for improvement.  The game gives you plenty of tools and lets you approach a situation however you like.  However the game favors certain types of play styles more than others.  Playing stealthy and taking everyone out non-lethally will give you the most XP, which means you can get more upgrades.  You can upgrade Jensen with praxis kits.  You get these praxis kits by getting enough XP or buy buying them in clinics.  There's plenty of stuff to upgrade but some of the augments you get are pretty useless.  For example "Smart Vision" allows you to see through walls.  Sounds pretty useful right?  It would be but the game has a Metal Gear Solid Style radar that lets you see enemies and their field of vision(with an upgrade) so it's actually pretty useless.  The only problem I had with the original HR was the boss fights.  Luckily the Boss fights have been fixed to an extent in the Directors Cut.  The PC port is good, no real problems except that tessellation can cause faces to be covered in white and black dots.
Score: 9/10

Step one...
If you're looking for a story mode review... scroll past, I haven't even touched it. Not at all.
To be fair, Balzblue gets a thumbs up because it works well for one, and looks great and runs smooth. It is a good fighting game that is complete and it adds elements that will probably get better over time.
However, for me, that's where it ends. For me, it feels like I'm playing soul calibur in 2d. Where certain characters can pretty much tap their way through all of your moves, or defeat you by actively countering all of your efforts and then relentlessly comboing you to death or near death and following up with the most bland way of killing you. And while it is obvious it needs to be a win or lose type of game, It does the game elements no justice at all to have regular ai in a game that could easily play insanely vibrantly like marvel vs capcom 3 or more accurately matrimelee.
Once you start playing or in my opinion, mashing, you'll notice Blazblue has tried their best to make every element count and have proper drawbacks, however, some more direct characters can actively push through the game with little to no technique, only to be floored by an ai that is akin to mugen making you suffer through some of the more tasteless but possible combos of the game. Things like rapid cancelling and air combos seem to have no proper airtime in the game although they could really REALLY show their stripes anywhere.
I don't know if they have stressed those mechanics in later games, And I do wish that the pc release has saw some sort of upgrade. However, as far as new fighting game IPs go, the later versions are usually large improvements over the last game, Though, when people boldly say Blazblue is the best 2d fighter made, I really want to ask them to name 5 fighting games and will flat out call them liars if they name any 2d fighting game with an intact air combo system. I hope they at least try to bring the latest release to steam and see what people do with it as a community, then actively fill in the gap of missing titles in the series... Because I am sure that this game is no longer an accurate summary of where the game has actually headed. And nobody is ever going to take the pc genre of the series seriously if most of the heavy hitters are just cash cows left to make devs direct income... showing from ill optimized titles like kof13 which pretty much runs like dry snot unless you can run games which actually need the power and skull girls which actually made a great anti piracy joke.
All in all, it is a fun game, however, there just doesn't feel like there's enough to leave this as a game in itself rather than another beat the ai title. Characters who are normally only for slapping around players who think you're going to do the obvious move or slash you into the cracks of the road are met with ai that is ready to grab your ankles to interrupt you and shoot a projectile while you're getting up to kill you off just as easy as they're willing to ground slash you as much as possible until you figure out it's basically soul calibur and unless you learn how to string together the foolproof-only-way-out-is-perfect-guard-combo, you'll be eating the equivalent down the line.

Jesus Christ half the review section is a sarcastic or straight-up offensive freaking blowtorch of disaster. Guys, I know you all want to find out how your Bulletshooter 1X452 4.3x7,54 submachinerifle works, but this is still a game. In order to get to the good bits, you need to PLAY and MASTER it, not rant about how you're too lazy to go through all the other portions of it.
If you're stuck grinding through the AK-47 then you're doing it wrong. To put it into perspective, I'm 15 hours into this and I have already unlocked around half the tech tree without even going back to a single gun nor paying for anything since it's meant to be a game where you play for 10-30 minutes and go back to your personal lives. It's a bit gimmicky and pretends to be a cow clicker game, but it's personally not that big of a grindfest when you start to take it for what it is.
If you're so desperate to learn about a particular gun then play the Quiz every 1-2 hours, I'm sure such a gun-nutter like you will definitely guess all the firearms it shows you and you will get the required Xp in no time. Try to get the "Champion" achievement on at least a few guns as well, like the TEC-9 or the Colt 1911 A1 or whatever it's called, it'll give you tons of Xp (It's not that hard, you just need a bit of practice, it's beneficial considering that it'll give you real-world knowledge of a particular weapon and how to best repair or dismantle it, because you never know when it might come in handy.)
It's an educational game, I am not good at firearms nor do I like them, but seeing how a lot of people are into it I might as well learn a bit about each weapon and its history. I do not know how accurate this game is, but for someone that has no prior knowledge of how even a flintock pistol works, I found it to be extremely well-made in terms of teaching you stuff. Even my dad learned how a Luger works with this, which is cool considering that he has a lot of knowledge about weapons.
All in all, I'm sick of seeing players who want someone to cherry-pick their favorite things without giving any effort for it. It's like playing an MMO and expecting to battle the final boss without even getting out of the tutorial level. Or wanting a girlfriend without going on a single date. Come on guys, you're better than that.

I've had a lot of fun with this game. It's a great installment in the series and offers some neat new ideas and twists on the previous games. Here are my key points in a nice short list:
(1) Technically the game seems to be very solid. I read quite a few worries about the PC build but I have not had any issues.  Of particular note, there are loads of options for tuning the game to your PC so its easy to strike the balance you want between FPS and visual fidelity. I managed to get a solid 60fps with custom settings that to my eye looked really nice.
(2) The sheet number of zombies on screen at once is stunning. I would guess there can be upward of five-hundred (500) of them at once in some of the larger areas. This is the first zombie game where you really feel like you are wading thought the creatures as they swarm after you.
(3) The combat is simple yet good fun. Its a basic light/heavy attack button masher. But its the weapons that make the game really fun. There is lots of variety ranging from the awesome to the daft. There is also a greatly expanded customization system which allows the creation of some really powerful and crazy means of destruction.
(4) The story is dumb but passable. Its a cheesey account of a few folks trying to escape the outbreak in a given city with some ham-fisted nonsense about goverment conspiracies tossed in for good measure. The characters are better than those in previous games but its still far from the highlight of the game. At best its a tacked on to give you an excuse to run around the city and deal with the zombies.
(5) As with the previous games there are some really off mysogynistic characters. In some ways they feel even more off the mark in this game where other characters are handled better. I guess at least not all the women are treated as freakish sexual objects but there are still some. I find it tasteless and pretty pathetic but I enjoy the rest of the game enough to overlook these issues.
All in all I enjoy the game a lot. At its best it is daft, fun, cool and mad all at once. It dips to some really pathetic lows with a few of the female characters which is a shame, yet not all that surprising coming from Capcom. However, aside from these few miss-steps its a pretty good game and well worth playing.
Oh, and its worth adding that it works perfeclty with the Xbox One controller via the wireless adapter. I mention this since the previous game did not work with a controller despite saying otherwise on the store page.

A beautiful game!
Truly one of the most unique styles I've ever seen in a game. Everything put into this game has its own depth, its own personality. Every land, character, song has been well planned and holds its own unique taste. Everything within this game has its own meaning, its own story, and its very interesting learning about each perspective you come across. The styles for the characters, objects, and areas of the game are really different. They all give me a sense of "I want to explore more! or I want to do more!" The atmosphere of this game is very beautiful!
Story: The story of the game, I'd say, is very unique, its different than anything I've ever encountered. At first, I belived that there was only one story to go through (2B's story), yet later, I found out that the story is a lot more vast than expected; there's a lot more to learn about the game. Each character has their own secrets, their own perspective to the world they live in, and you get your own intake about each one. I find that very immersive and well liked.
Gameplay: Now the gameplay is very skewed for me. Personally, I believe that it could get repetitive at times, sometimes you'll have to go out farming in order to level up in order to achieve battles that require a higher level, but each battle holds its own personality and is very different than other battles. I wouldn't say that makes up the repetitiveness, but it doesn't get so boring that it'll stop curiosity.
Atmosphere: The game really captures you, I believe that everything just ties together so well with one another, each land having its own personality, yet still being a part of what the entire game is about. The music for each land you enter holds its own story and I find it really interesting and enjoyable. Everything contains a purpose, personality, individual traits and aspects, and thats what makes the atmosphere very captivating.
This game is truly astonishing, I fully recommend it (:

The Great Fusion is a story set in a near future, where the economical crisis has taken a turn for a worse, making all countries fusionned in one, where riches are richer and where poors are poorer. And the copyright has taken over the world. You're Max, a geek, that lost his job at the beginning of the crisis and despite working, he's depressed and in a poor district. One day, Mate, his friend, finds a CD with Pong on it. But after playing it, Mate is kidnapped.... It's your job to find him!
It's a point-&-click game, with a depressing setting... but also satirical. In reality, the whole story is a parody (and also denouncing) of the mighty copyright. A lot of 'easter eggs' can be found: Larry for Leisure suit Lary, the boss that loves cats, the thugs whose names are directly a reference to video games, etc.. There is however no puzzles apart to find all objects and use them.
The problem of the game is the lack of real objective. There is no indication of what to do. Unless you find the right character to speak with. Also, you can't control your save. If you missed an achievement, you have to begin again the game.
The translation, while very good, has some spelling mistakes. I played the game in French by the way. So, it's also multi-language.
The graphics are cartoonish, reinforcing the comedy settings. The soundtrack is also good.
I got the game through a bundle and I don't regret it. However, to fully enjoy the game, you must have also a good reference of culture (cinema, arts, video games). I'm pretty sure I missed some jokes. I recommend it mainly for people loving adventure games. It may bore others.

I wish that  under "Do you recommend this game?" between the "Yes" and "No" buttons, there would be one called "Meh".  The Great Fusion is a nice looking, well made game, but while the game feature list includes "Current affairs remarks with nods to social criticism", the game is so left leaning that I got a cramp in my neck from playing it.  Don't get me wrong, I certainly agree with some of the general sentiment, and I'm as aware of income and privilege disparity as poor people tend to be, but by the end of this game, I was starting to feel like it was written by Noam Chomsky and Alex Jones.
Aside from what sort of message the game may or may not be trying to convey, Is it fun?  I did play through the whole game, but it never really felt all that fun.  A lot of walking back and forth, dragging things over other things, hoping one of them would work, all the while being presented with a series of stereotypical caricatures such as "the greedy landlord", "the stupid boss", "the corrupt cop", or "the blind fish seller".  Ok, well that last one wasn't all that stereotypical, but anwyay.

The Great Fusion does try to be funny, and falls rather flat there as well, since it feels like every attempt at humor is pasted over the "message" the game is trying to deliver, besides the gags just not being funny in the first place.  I liked the bit about getting the rat to wash the dishes, but the funniest part is that the entire game is about how copyright protection and enforcement pretty much destroyed civilization as we know it, and I bought the game on Steam.

All in all, though, not a bad game.

This is, in my honest opinion, the best hardcore racing simulator in the market. If you are looking for a racing simulator with very good and convincing physics, excellent force feedback and a most complete package of cars then you should buy this. If you are determined to buy only one racing simulator, then you should definately buy AMS. No other game comes close to the variety of cars and series that you can race in AMS. It has plenty of classic and modern tracks with some unique ones that you will not find elsewhere.
Not saying that there are no negatives, the lack of VR support is one thing that a minority of people regard as a must. The graphics are also a little dated in comparison with the competition, but the game really looks beatiful. And, if you are a hardcore racing simulation lover, then you know graphics come second to physics simulation, which this game excels at.
For multiplayer racing, you will need to participate in some community leagues to get regular online races, as public servers are mostly empty.
In the other hand, for singleplayer races and championships, honestly, this is the only choice for you currently. As no other hardcore simulator offer all the options of making a race or even a full season as Automobilista does. The recently released season tool is just the icing on the cake. The AI after the latest updates is simply phenominal. Not even RF2 highly praised AI can compete with Automobilista's AI, Let alone the very inferior AI of other games such as AC or PC1 & PC2.
And while the game lacks weather support, it does have full day/night cycles and varius options to control time progression throughout a racing weekend.
This is a true definition of an underrated gem in it's genre. Frankly, just do yourself a favor and buy it if you have any interest in any racing discipline, as this game has them all.

I have been playing this game for over a year, and I have over 1.5k hours on it. In the beginning, this game was super fun, there were a lot of different champs with different playstyles. There were different ways you can play each champ, so basically just a lot of customization. The game was relatively skill-based where a good player would be able to win most of his/her games.
Having said all this, the direction this game is heading in is absolutely the wrong direction. The next update that is meant to come out at the time I am writing this is OB 64, and with this update, the game has spelled its end. I say this because the game has become too reliant on microtransactions.
Each champion in this game has a set of cards that define his/her playstyle, and you can guess that these cards are vital to the playstyle of the champ. Before OB 64, players were able to unlock any card customize its level within the specific loadout. What Hi-Rez has done now is make it so that all these cards are unlocked for you already but the individual levels of these cards can only be increased by getting duplicates of these cards.
To obtain duplicates, unsurprisingly, you must open loot boxes. According to a source on reddit, it would talk you
984,000 gold to upgrade a set of cards to their max level for ONE champion, and there are a total of 34 champions in the game as of now. To put this into perspective, you earn around 300-500 gold per match, so yeah, calling it a grind is an understatement. You could expect this level of grind in an MMORPG, but not in a hero shooter.
But, if you're willing to pay for crystals to unlock these chests, then you can get a quick headstart on other players. The reason for this is Hi-Rez is marketing this game in China. The Chinese playerbase love microtransactions, and so Hi-Rez has made this patch in anticipation of the influx of Chinese players.
To be fair, there is a competitive mode where everyone has the same level cards, but this only means that you are not bale to practice your champions in a casual mode, and there is also the fact that players are used to having some cards at different levels.
All in all, this game is dying, Hi-Rez does not care about its playerbase, and don't play this game.
Also, check out these reviews of Hi-Rez, makes it look like a pretty good company, huh?

As a fan of Arc System Works' previous Guilty Gear games, and also having watched
, I've long been meaning to give BlazBlue a shot. I'm a fairly casual fighting game player and mostly play Street Fighter, but I found BlazBlue easy to get into, and I love how uniquely each character plays. Ragna feels like a pretty standard melee character and is a good way to get used to how to the game works, but then you also get characters like Nu, who doesn't play like anything I've ever seen before, with a focus on ranged attacks without the use of complex inputs. The cast is a little smaller than I'd like, but this is unavoidable due to the age of the game; unfortunately we have yet to see any PC ports past the first game.
The art and sound design are also top-notch, just as they were in Guilty Gear, though this game is considerably more modern and much prettier graphically than the even more aged Guilty Gear titles available on PC. Game runs well too, with a pretty steady 60 FPS even on my fairly weak machine. There's no online multiplayer, but for someone like me who tends to get walked all over online in fighting games by the people who play the game more seriously, that's fine by me. In addition to the arcade mode, which does have little clips of story here and there, there's also a full-fledged story mode that plays out like a visual novel and adds some content to help keep things from getting stale.
Overall BlazBlue is probably going to be my go-to fighting game going forward. It's not perfect, but I've been enjoying my time with it immensely (especially Noel's combos, my God). The only thing this game is missing as far as I'm concerned is
If that song played every Bang fight, no, every fight, no, at all times, I would be a happy man.

TL;DR: It's TF2 if everybody is scout and uses some terribly op version of the rocket launcher. Also, grinding.
This game interested me with its weapon crafting and sense of humor. I liked TF2 well enough, so I figured, hey, why not give this a shot? I downloaded it.
After four tries, the game finally actually works. What kind of game can't change resolution while it's up? I've never had that happen before. It astounds me. I tried to move on, however.
The first thing I was disappointed by was the lack of a tutorial or any sort of bot mode (but the game itself does have bots in regular games, so what the hell is up with that?). The only way you can test your weapons is to shoot at static targets or targets that move in a straight line. This is incredibly useless because all actual humans do is jump around like a scared rabbit. They do that because it's easy and it works. Anyway...
So I just decide to not prematurely spend any Blutes and go with a basic rifle/launcher with no added parts. I join a match, and they seem to work well enough. Well, the rifle at least. No aiming required, really, and with 50 ammo it's hard to ♥♥♥♥ up.
I played a few matches. I noticed that the whole "weapon part exp" thing was progressing extremely slowly and that it would take several dozen matches to get anywhere at all. I also saw that most players used multi-launchers and spamable tesla things. I decided to spend the vast majority of my Blutes on something different but interesting, then -- a remote-detonated corkscrew single rocket, and a pulse shotgun. They worked well enough in the test zone (which, in hindsight, is garbage). So then I went into a match with them.
They sucked. Both of them were countered easily by the strategy of jumping around aimlessely and firing multi-launchers in my general direction.
This game is terribly, awfully unbalanced. Beam is the most worthless thing, and, again, the only things that are of worth are multi-launchers and perhaps elemental rifles. If you want to play a game that boasts on its weapon customizations, and makes the huge majority of these customizations worthless, AND wastes your progression with a ♥♥♥♥ing worthless way to test them, then this is the game for you. If you want to play something where people don't all use the same weapons, and for a ♥♥♥♥ing good reason, then look elsewhere.

I'm far too uneducated, and immature, to really break down and analyze this game. Take the review with a grain of salt, please.
If ever there were a testement to games being an artform, this would be it. Some people find music to sing what they don't have the words to speak. Some people use color to illustrate what they feel deep inside. Some people like sex.
This game is far more mature than the arguably juvenile overexposure of adult themes, partial nudity and constant barrage of vague sexual references would grant in a first impression. Games are an artform, and this game stands in the highest pantheon for me. Color used beautifully to set moods. Songs used to sing words I could never quite speak. Sexy androids to ogle.
Every part of the human experience is touched upon in this game. Physical senses. Birth, Life, Death, sentience, self awareness.
I'd fail here if I didn't at least touch on the adult themes and partial nudity in this game. Yes, the game contains far too much partial nudity for any game one would normally take seriously. What the game seems to try and hammer home at every chance it gets is that lust is a human experience and can often drive or differentiate the emotion we call love. What's pleasing to the eyes, or to the touch, it's part of what makes us human. You may find yourself literally stopping to smell the flowers, or taking in the sights through your digital android eyes. If you at any point find yourself stopping to stare at the sights, android body or scenery, just know that it makes you human.
The search for meaning in life seems to be the main theme in this game, but by virtue of being a game you of course have set goals. Much like the androids you play as. Scan the region, eliminate the hostile threat. Retake Earth for the humans. Two very different methods of creation. Creation for a purpose like that of a hammer for a nail, or creation without purpose. Like that of man.
There are so many small story arcs woven in through the grand arcs and such beautiful realizations that I couldn't fully appreciate until I had finished the 3rd playthrough and started anew. One small arc had turned out to affect my entire personal life after the fact. For better or worse, my life has changed since I played this game, but this is one kid's anecdote. Remember games are made to be played, have fun.

Just like its description, this is pretty much a beat'em up game but it certainly involves some battle tactics like jumping, dodging, item uses, etc. Players start with adventurer and proceed to unlock other classes after completing some achievements. What makes the game addictive is that as players go deeper, rooms are getting more difficult with more enemies and enemies that attack quite often, but by completing some achievements they grant players some better start-off stats as well as better utility throughout the whole run. It took me at least 15 hours to complete all those achievements that gives actual benefit in battle and survival, and I did plan ahead before I play so it might take even longer for casual players.
What's after the achievements? They've got difficult areas such as Arena where you fight waves of monsters and try to survive, Endless dungeon which is really tricky to survive with curses and disease that you MUST take in later floors, Shadow World with insane difficulty and random classes with random stats which is quite challenging.
I do highly recommend playing this game with a friend online or local because it has so much more fun than just playing it alone. I wish the game could have a larger item pool with more randomization as well as more weapons and fighting styles that can lead to better variety in battle.
