I have to say first off that my opinion may be considered biased as this was the first mmo rpg that I  truly loved. I had played WoW previously and couldn't stick with it, so when I saw this game I was less than optimistic, however I am jubilant to inform you that this game captured both my attention as well as my imagination.
Part of this is the art style, I am a huge fan of anime in general and this games aethestic was the whole reason I started my adventure as an envoy of Gaia. But my love for anime wasn't the only artistic point within this game, the enemies that you encounter are well designed and truly fun to throw down with, not only that but the areas and dungeons in this game are so beautiful and imaginative that it's hard not to just stare around at random pretty scenes going "oooh" and "ahhh".
Another strong point in this game are the eidolons that follow you about, helping you beat the local wildlife into lumps of exp. The eidolons are a core focus of the game, you start the game with one of four, I always choose Merilee the cheery silph, others include a dragon, a floating boy, and a unicorn straight out of my little pony. The eidolons are upgradable too, so they progress with you, and can be passed around between your charecters at will, as long as they're not assigned to a charecter already.
The final good point I'm going to make, I had a few more but I'm getting lazy, is the games intricate story, now on the outside this game looks cutezie and nice, but read some diologue and you quickly realize this game is about as serious as knee surgery. Espionage, robberery, demons, a scandolouse love story in the second area, and the tragic tale of a theif, whom I will not name. It's a real shame that most people skip the diologue, it's rich and interesting and makes the game much better than withought it, ie nothing would make any sense.
Now for the bad news, if you want endgame, too bad. Of course  there's the sky tower a raid right in the main hub of the game, and with the most recent update came the sky realms, of which I know nothing about because my internet recently gave out. I love this game but the severe lack of endgame content needs to be fixed.
Another negative is the gut renching grind your looking at if you want eidolons that you can't get through the story. Basically you need key fragments, 8 of them if my memory serves, now that doesn't sound bad until you realize that to get the key fragments you have to defeat that eidolon in boss form only to realize that the drop rate for the fragments are ridiculously miniscule. In short only go for eidolons you really want. Or just pay for the keys in the game store with real money....
My final point of negativity is the charecter levels 60-62. If your a veteran you know what I mean, dear lord it takes so much to get to lv 62, you have to do both areas unlocked at these levels twice to three times through to gain the necessary exp. It takes way too long to go up those two levels.
Well I hope you find this review helpful, please give this game a chance, it's great and it needs more love from Western players. Thanks for reading.

You can skip it and go out on adventures, kill some raiders, get better armor, meet companions, and come back with power armor and chain guns and just massacre the slavers.  You could free the slaves, or become a slaver, and that will dramatically change a lot in how the game plays.  This is not something you can do in games with level adustment and relatively "on the rails" plot.  You can decide maybe you don't care that much about your friend and just not bother with it at all; you're missing the next "step" in the plot but Fallout doesn't really work that way.  The plot is more organic and flexible.  You feel like you're telling a story rather than being told a story.  You can go get married, join a cult, get into drug smuggling, become of citizen of one of the major powers, become a porn star, go back to your hometown who sent you out on your quest and kill them all, and forget about saving them from some stupid drought.
I'm pretty picky about my video games, but this is one of those games that it doesn't matter who you are, what kinds of games you like, or even if you hate video games.  Make an exception here.  Even if it's not your thing, it's interesting to see what they did here.

If you want to have a stark contrast in how much gaming has evolved over the years, then place this 2016 version of
side by side with the 1993 version of this game. The differences is startling in multiple aspects not only in the gameplay and graphics, but also the hardware that is required to run this game.
Around July, 2017, the game released it’s 6.66 patch, made all the DLC free, and was on sale for $15 (USD). This was a must-purchase. I played through the campaign mode at the “Hurt Me Plenty” settings, and it took me nine hours to get through the entire campaign. Unfortunately, the campaign storyline is on the weakest part of this game. When I got to the end, it was just “the end” with no conclusion, and no satisfactory resolution.
The graphics and gameplay, however, are excellent. I was able to get consistent 90 FPS (or higher) during the game play at 2560×1440 resolution, although I think this game is an excellent advertisement for a adaptive sync monitor. What I especially enjoyed is the “glory kill” feature which, once you weakened the enemy enough, you can perform a melee attack to rip the enemy apart and, in the process, get some health and some ammo.
What insures the replayability of this game is the same reason why the original
was played for several years: community maps. These custom maps allow for additional gameplay, and many a game designer got their start from custom maps from the original game.
For this old gamer, however, 24 years has passed, and my reactions aren’t what they are used to be. I won’t even try to compete with the younger kids who play
now.

So I put off writing this review for a while, having recieved my controller the week of launch. I wanted to give myself time, and if one thing comes across from this review, it's that you should GIVE THIS CONTROLLER TIME. The steam controller is now central to my gaming time, but it didn't start that way.
When I recieved the controller I was excited, and also very impressed with it. It's a sexy piece of hardware. I immediatly pulled up Batman Arkham Knight (what I was playing at the time) and felt the ground drop from under me. I found it uncomfortable, the trackpads were weird, I kept missing buttons. I paniced a little. I had invested alot of hope in the controller, so I launched Rocket League, picked a config and started playing. It was beautiful, and on top of that it was exactly what I imiagined it would be when I bought the controller.
Thus I concluded that the controller would work for some games, just not for all of them. And I was right, but for the wrong reasons.
My transition with the Steam Controller mirrors what happened when I began using linux for work. Things weren't where I was expecting them. It felt different, and while I could see how there was alot of potential, I couldn't see how to take advantage of it.
But you know something, after four weeks of playing Rocket League and adventure games I went back to Arkham Knight and got a higher combo multiplier than I ever that with my previous controller.
This thing is amazing, but it's different. Take time to learn what it is, and what it is not (and how it works) and it will be the best controller you ever own.

Simply an amazing game.
The story is pretty interesting. The premise is you're an android and you beat up alien robots in the future. You're fighting for humanity's survival. Although it starts out slow, it ramps up in intensity as it goes on and I was blown away by the time the game ended.
As far as combat goes, it's a standard Platinum game. It is extremely fluid and fun with a well-implemented dodge system. You feel powerful beating up robots. One unique aspect is that there's a leveling system, but it is pretty barebones as it just results in stat increases. But, you can greatly customize your playstyle with a variety of different weapons and equipment. You're given a few large areas to explore with several side-quests to do everywhere. Although a few were rather simple and boring, many of the side-quests were actually pretty interesting and brought in some more context about main story events.
Music is outstanding.
The graphics for this game are also very good, due to great art direction. Although some textures are a bit low-res, it still looks really nice especially on high settings.
The biggest issue with this game is performance, because the PC port isn't perfect. For some people, the game simply doesn't work, and there are some fullscreen and white-screen issues. Most of these issues are fixed with the FAR mod, so definitely check that out. It also provides a ton of options to fine-tune the game. I'm running on a laptop with a GTX 960M and an i7-6700HQ cpu, and I was able to get a pretty consistent 50-60 FPS on medium settings with the FAR mod.
Overall, I would highly recommend this game. It is one of the best games I've played in a while. And yes, there are butts.
TL;DR: It's Bayonetta if Bayonetta was an open-world RPG about beating the crap out of robots.

This game is outstanding by more than one parameters, but I think its best side is the multi-choice storyline. To a reasonable extent the game offers you many ways to reach goals, and to slightly alter the storyline with your decisions, while keeping the integrity, not turning the story into a mess like some RPGs tend to do. You can play the game like a shooter, or avoid killing people. You can use stealth or go into a direct confrontation. You can hack doors or break through walls or find secret passages. Designers managed to push into the levels so many ways to reach the destination, without turning it into a chaos. Writers managed to do the same with the story. It's a clever game made by clever people.
The Director's Cut version of the game, however, is one step forward, two steps back. Although it does introduce alternative ways to defeat enemies during boss fights, but also, it introduces many bugs not present in the original version. I think that it also makes the game easier, at least I had more upgrades than I needed. It might be a nice thing for people who found the game too difficult, but I wouldn't say it was necessary. The worst thing is that it integrates The Missing Link DLC into the main game story. This decision was evidently NOT made by the game's director, because the DLC does not fit the main game. It was made afterwards, probably written afterwards, and was intended to be played afterwards. It's less polished, has a different feel to it, requires different tactics and has its own story arc. It should have stayed as a DLC. Luckily, I own both original and director's cut versions.
In spite of flaws introduced by Director's Cut, it is still a very, very good game. It is a shame the makers didn't have a budget to polish it and get rid of the bugs, and were forced to include The Missing Link DLC as a marketing measure.
So, I give the game itself 10/10, but the Director's Cut version gets 8/10.
Don't get me wrong this game is a good time burner but there are so many better games that can fufil this with so much more enjoyment, after a while it becomes repetative and boring.

Writing a review for such a big and pretty lenghty game is challenging. In my opinion, this is a game that should be talked about amongst friends and choices they made throughout the game and their own moral standing regarding technology and it´s influence on modern society.
Deus Ex: Human Revolution is a prequel to the first game in the Deus Ex series, Deus Ex from 2000. The story is set in 2027, 25 years before the events of the original Deus Ex, and in the center of it all is an ex-swat trying to find out the truth behind the curtain of lies, deceit and conspiracy, while simultaneously dealing with his own personal loss and tragedy. This tragedy  will define him ( or better yet, YOU, the PLAYER ) as a person and his own moral take on science and technology.
The gameplay, itself, is pretty varied and offers a number of ways on how to complete an objective, whether you prefer stealth, hacking, action or, even, social interaction. That type of gameplay nicely corresponds with the story since in Human Revolution everything is about choice and exploration. Whether your choices/your exploration really mattered at the end.....well....that´s up to YOU to decide.
Since I haven´t played the first Deus Ex and it´s sequel Invisible War, I can´t say that the game is worthy of it´s predecessors, but what I can say is that I really enjoyed this game in it´s 35 hour run and I definitely recommend this game to anyone interested in cyber-punk type game in which your choices paint the story and, in a way, maybe, YOU.

My favorite game of all time. Just... wow. Where to begin?
Well, the basic premise of the game is that you take the roll of Adam Jensen: an ex-cop and current security manager of Sarif Industries, a leading developer of controversial augmentations, which allow a person to be genetically and mechanically enhanced in almost any way possible. You are witness to a massacre and mysterious raid on a Sarif Plant where he and his girlfriend work, and you search to find out what happened, and where the scientists and Megan, your girlfriend, have gone, if they are even still alive. And as you go on, encountering key players in the government, augmentation industry, and military powers, the conspiracy grows deeper, starting to reveal a darker intent that expands into almost every facet of human society.
Needless to say, the story is phenomenal: with gameplay and conversation based-choices that impact how the story progresses, and what others think of you, this game lets you play it the way YOU want to, not just as some on-rails shooter like Call of Duty, both based on Story and Gameplay. This game will make you think, not just about how to approach obstacles, but about what is 'right and wrong' in how humanity must evolve, what actually makes us human? How far must we go to get what we want, even if others might get hurt in the process, and more.
Specifically about the gameplay: you can play this game, much like the original, in just about any way imaginable. Lethally or non-lethally, stealthily or guns-blazing, or even solving problems without having to knock anyone out or killing anyone, just by proper communication through the persuasion of who you are talking to. Outnumbered and outgunned, you can use many routes to accomplish your goal, using vents, moving heavy objects, back alleys, even hacking computer terminals to open doors, disable cameras, and turn turrets and robots off OR against your enemies.
There are a variety of weapons and tools, from standard weaponry like pistols and rifles, to laser weaponry and even non-lethal guns like the Tranquilizer Rifle and Stun Gun. Each weapon can be upgraded through weapon mods you buy and find hidden in levels, and also, just about every aspect of your character can be upgraded: from health, to shooting, even hacking and taking out multiple enemies with melee attacks.
Put into simple words: this game is played how YOU want to play it, performing actions and making choices based on your preferences of playstyle and even ethics. You do what you feel is right, and what you feel needs to be done to reach your goal in a world full of risks, people who will lie, decieve, and manipulate, where conspiracies are abundant in a technologically advanced world, that shows that even with advances in the world around us, humanity itself will always face the same problems that they must overcome, in trying times of uncertainty.
A instant classic that you simply NEED to play. Especially if it is on sale. This game is worth playing: it's a smart, sexy, classy FPS and RPG hybrid that nails the story, atmosphere, soundtrack, and gameplay in just about every way imaginable, and is my all-time favorite game that deserves to be experienced.

Deus Ex: Human Revolution is a very good game which succeeds in bringing the fascinating Deus Ex universe into the newer generation of games and gamers. It excels primarily in two areas. Firstly, the stealth gameplay is very enjoyable and with consequences depending on whether or not one chooses to kill or merely subdue one's enemies. The levelling system (through human augmentation) is also very interesting and continually provides new dynamics to the gameplay, keeping it fresh. The fact that there are also many different paths leading to one's mission goals which may or may not be accessible due to one's playing style and where one chooses to spend one's augments is also a welcome achievement in an age of increasingly linear RPG titles.
The best feature of Deus Ex: Human Revolution, however, just like its predecessors, is the storyline. The truly believeable dystopian not-so-distant future in which humans have to decide how they stand towards their own improvement through augmentations is transferred faithfully into Human Revolution along with all of its ethical and moral dilemmas. This reviewer, for one, regrets that the developers did not play more on the main protagonist's conflict between initially disliking augments and being forced without his consent to have them. It is the backstory, rather than the immediate one and its characters which makes the game truly interesting. Nonetheless, this is a feature that adds significantly to the appeal of this title.
All in all, Human Revolution is a very good game. There are a few ways in which it could have been improved dramatically to become a true classic of our times. However, with solid gameplay and a great storyline, Deus Ex: Human Revolution is definitely worth your time. 8.5/10.

My experience... I have been driving Grand Prix Legends since it was released in 1998. I have tried iRacing, fFactor 2, and Assetto Corsa. In my opinion Automobilista is a more realistic driving experience than all of them. From my first session on track I was convinced. Now that I've spent some more time dialing things in, I'm hooked. When you first start out, be sure to take the time to peruse the "user guide". The physics and ffb had me convinced immediately but the graphics were washed out. After reading the "user guide" on configuring Nvidia/ATI graphics cards and applying the recommended settings, the graphics are very good. The ffb is the best I have experienced. I'm still using my old faithful Logitech Momo Red wheel and an even older, modded, set of Thrustmaster pedals with a Flexiforce load sensor on the brake. I was going to test drive Project Cars but there's no need. I am quite happy with Automobilista. I would recommend Automobilista to anyone who is looking for a sim with realistic handling and feedback. If you are looking for more of an arcade experience, there is nothing to see here.
Some thoughts on:
iRacing... I quite liked iRacing but for me the ffb was not very good. A bit like driving underwater. I tried different settings but never found anything I was satisfied with. That said; I would stay with iRacing just for the sheer number of online races that are available, except for the cost. Ongoing subscription and then track and car purchases to move up the ranks are too much for me.
rfactor 2... Great graphics but physics and ffb just seem unrealistic to me.
Assetto Corsa... I thought the graphics in rfactor 2 were better on my 32" monitor. AC was too sparkly and I was unable to adjust to eliminate the sparkles. And again the physics and ffb weren't realistic to me.
Final thought... of course all of this is subjective and may largely depend on your rig.

While I've been a fan of this series ever since my friend told me about it a couple years ago, I never actually played any of the games due to not having a PS3 or an Xbox 360. I know that this game was on PC over in the UK and on GFWL and such, but I never bothered to get that since I didn't feel like it was worth it, not to mention the price. So when I saw this on steam, I jumped at the chance. I DID take a look at the steam information on this game and I still bought it. So let's get on with the good and the bad.
:
-
. I really like the sprites and detailed backgrounds in the stages. I'm not the sort of guy who thinks games are only as good as their graphics. Not at all. But the game's graphics is a plus for me.
-
. I think everyone already knows that pretty much every game has at least some good music. Fighting games generally have awesome music. You get the OST when you buy this game and it's so worth it.
-
. I've played 9.6 hours as of this review, and I'm not even halfway done with the story. The story has branching paths depending on whether you win, lose, win with a distortion/astral heat, or choose different options in the story when the choice arises (There's a guide in the community hub to help you get 100% on all character's stories). There's only three characters that have an astral heat when you first start the game. To get the others, you have to beat arcade mode with the character you want the astral heat for. You can also unlock Unlimited mode for characters, which just makes them more powerful, by having more speed, power, modified distortions, etc. That also adds a bit more to the length. Beside that, there's also score attack to do and the gallery to complete if you wanted to do those things.
-
. You get all of this for $10. I think I got like at least $20 worth from playing some of the character's stories and listening to the OST alone.
:
-
. For me, I don't really care too much that this game doesn't have online versus. I know that fighting games are really all about playing against someone else and most places don't have a local fighting scene. However I will say that online play is never recommended for top play. It's fine for beginner-intermediate play, but there's always some sort of latency that to play extremely competitively online in a fighting game is sort of absurd. But while I don't care too much that it's offline only, I still would've liked to see it have online. H2 Interactive might be able to implement it in the future.
-
. This is a straight port of the GFWL version, so all the bugs on there are also on here. Sometimes your game will be locked at 30 FPS if your computer's been on for a while. This can easily be fixed with a restart. When I first started the game, the FPS was actually locked at around 17 FPS, but again restarting my computer fixed that. There's also a bug for some people where story mode does not have music at all. If you alt+tab out of the window and come back in, sometimes the characters' sprites will be invisible or have weird hitbox colors. These can usually be fixed if you alt+tab again or have the sprites change (either by hitting, getting hit, or anything else that changes the sprites). Same thing happens in story mode's cutscenes. Alt+tabbing will usually make the character completely invisible, or partly invisible, and the only way for that to be fixed is if the character moves somehow due to an event in the story. But it'll only happen for that one scene you alt+tabbed out of. It may also crash on certain parts, I've read about how some people are crashing after clearing score attack but I haven't played that mode yet.
-
. Despite it saying Full controller support, it only fully supports Xbox controllers and anything using Xbox. My PS2 controller doesn't work, but my Madcatz TE Xbox 360 stick
. For any other controllers, you'll have to find a way to emulate the Xbox 360 controller or maybe use one of those controller mapping programs. I have no experience with those so I'm just glad I got an Xbox 360 stick instead of a PS3 one (Though I would very much like to have one still).
-
. There's absolutely no tutorial on what you can do. There
a manual if you right click the game and read it (but who really does that? I didn't even know about it until I right clicked it once). So you'll have to either go into training mode and test out your things or read a guide or something. Basically each character has a light attack, medium attack, and heavy attack, recognized as A, B, and C respectively. Each character also has a Drive attack, recognized as D. Every single attack also has a forward+ action, so if you hold forward and press A, B, C, or D, you'll do a different attack than just pressing A, B, C, or D by itself. Same thing for in the air, though I believe it depends on certain characters. Arakune, for example, has a down+A/B/C attack in the air. Pressing A+B at the same time gives you a barrier block, which is different from a normal block, obviously. There's also an instant block and instant barrier block, if you block about 8 frames before an attack connects. B+C is your grab attack. A+B+C consumes 50 heat, and allows you to cancel a move. A+B+C+D is your burst, which lets you get out of a combo. Not recommended to use early in the round, since you won't have a barrier gauge and will be in Danger status until the round ends. However, definitely recommended if you're supposed to lose in story mode to get a certain scene or path.
Overall, I would still recommend this game. If you have never played a BlazBlue game but wanted to, I'd say go for it. If you want to experience the story, go for it. If you want to get familiar with BlazBlue games, go for it (Although each new game changes something). Despite the cons, I still really enjoyed the game and will enjoy it for many more hours to come. The story and OST alone are worth the $10, I'd say.

It's the ultimate Freespace experience.

Dead Rising 3 has received quite the negative reputation over it's course of existance. The only thing is, I can't agree with it's negative feedback.
From someone who enjoyed both Dead Risings 1 and 2 on the Xbox 360, the transition over was very nice if I do say so myself (from Xbox to PC). People claim this is a very "poor port" but yet this game runs flawlessly on my

without a single issue. Before I mention anything else about performance, please realize that I DID unlock the frame cap and I enabled Vsync because this game suffers pretty badly from screen tearing. I might also add that my system is pretty

(I'll add my specs at the bottom of the review
).
I guess since I'm already talking about performance, I'll start off straight away with that. This game DOES have a frame lock at 30, but you can download and add a .ini file from a website (I'm too lazy to get the link) that offers the file. Other than that, the game runs very smoothly without any real major dips in framerates. Users have complained about frame dips, but like I said, I didn't experience anything major. Zombie hordes do lower my FPS by about 5 or 10 FPS, but it usually kicks right out of it and by the time it does that it's almost completely unnoticable. Regardless, the game can hold a 60 FPS very nicely. Some people have also complained about crashing- in the time I've played it, I haven't experienced a single crash yet.
My only real complaints for this game are the controls and it's lack to sometimes render small objects that are mere feet away. The controls feel very poorly done, especially with the camera. The manual mouse movement feels slow and laggy almost. Using WASD to move around also feels like it's delayed or something. Using a controller would probably feel better, but as far as keyboard/mouse, I think it just needs some getting used to. I haven't played a Dead Rising game for a couple of years, so it might just be me getting used to the controls again. Regarding the rendering with some objects, notice that I stress "sometimes" because this only happens very seldom. Most of the times I forget about it- in fact, I'm actually editing my review after I wrote this to add this in because I completely forgot about it.
Compared to other Dead Rising games, you're not stranded in a god forsaken mall. You're set in a fairly open world environment with lots of backroads and the sorts. Lots of areas in the map are open and are accessable. I read somewhere that "90% of the doors are locked in the game" but yet I've only seen two locked doors- and they were apart of a mission where they were SUPPOSED to be locked... DR3 takes on a nice and new approach and I think they did a great job with it so far.
DR3 also added in a better (imo) crafting (or 'combo' system as they call it) system and way more vehicles. They added in craftable cars and combo-cars as well. You can combo weapons and things found through blueprints, just as in Dead Rising 2. Blueprints are scattered across the map, along with PP collectables and more, all of which are located on the minimap in the corner (which is nice). Unlike DR1 and DR2, the time system is MUCH more leanient. I still have a few missions from when I started the game that I haven't even touched, yet I still have over 75% of my time remaining.

576 hours and less than 5 months later, I have beaten the game.  I have done what I once thought was impossible.  At first I thought my life was complete.  But now that it is all over, I feel rather empty inside.  Nothing will be the same without AdCap.  Meaning to life no longer exists.
HOW TO BEAT THE GAME.
It is fairly simple now that I look back on it.  Put all of your eggs into Earth.  Yes, it is important to work on other planets but DO NOT SPEND GOLD OR MEGABUCKS ON THEM UNTIL YOU MAX OUT EARTH.  This is very important, as it will affect your future.
To beat Earth you must first beat Mars.  Do not buy individual golden tickets for any planet.  Always save up and buy the 10 pack (you will thank me later).
Once mars is beaten and you have Earth decked out in platinum, keep it going.  Pump all of your megabucks into maxing earth out.  Once this is done, you can start work on upgrading the moon.  UPGRADE MARS LAST (very important).
If you get any kind of gold, save it.  Once you can get a micromanager for earth, do so.  Only upgrade that.  If you can, get the x2 speed boost suit afterwards.  Beat all of the events.  Sometimes you have to spend the gold you would/earn from them to boost them to get to the megabucks they offer, this is definitely worth it.  But do NOT spend more gold than is earned in the event, this is very important.
Clicker games were built for autoclickers.  Why?  Because no one wants to spend several years manually clicking things.  Once you have Earth's micromanager up, go to sleep with the game on and your autoclicker at the ready.
So you have beaten Earth.  Congrats!  Now you have an awesome option.  Reset.  Do it.  You get 5000 gold for doing so.  That 5000 gold is your ticket to beating the moon!  I was able to beat the moon less than an hour after resetting earth.
You beat the game!  Now what?  I don't know.  I don't know...............

WOW!  All I can say is ............. WOW!  iRacing, watch out.  This game currently cost 30 bucks with no residual cost (as of this writing).
Let's talk racing simulation.
1. Car physics.  Automobilista has nailed it!  The different cars have different physics and handling characteristics that you can feel!  Tire wear, suspension travel, brakes, camber.....you make adjustments and you feel the difference.
2. Dynamic tracks and tire wear. I swear while I was racing in the F3 car I could see my tires degrading over time............not just feel it but see it.  Now, maybe it's just because you have real time telemetry data that tells you what your tire state is, but I kept looking at my right front tire and I could swear I started seeing tread wear. Anyway, they have their tire model spot on.........and it's only going to get better.  The tires pick up gravel and grass if you run off the road and you can hear it on the pavement also.  Run behind someone that has ran off the road and hear the dirt and gravel ping and pong off your car's underbelly.  Great job.
3.  Force Feedback.  THIS RIGHT HERE PEOPLE IS WHAT FORCE FEEDBACK IS ALL ABOUT.  They got it right..........on the first try none the less.  There are a number of default setups for almost every racing wheel you can think of.  G27, G29, MoMo, driving force..........if you have a wheel, it's probably supported here.  (CAUTION:  This is a TRUE racing sim, so please don't attempt to drive with a gamepad.  I see some support is in there, but you really are not going to get the full experience).
4.  Graphics.  This is where some pundants say that Automobilista is failing.  I say that they are a small team of developers with a small budget that have created a simulation that is DIRECTLY  challenging Assetto Corsa, iRacing, RFactor, etc.  If I was to put the graphics to a scale of 1-10, I'd give them a solid 7.............but remember, this is an Early Access of the game.  How may of you remember Assetto Corsa's early access. Pretty damn strong graphics........horrible physics.  Automobilista is headed in the right direction.
5.  AI.  I know, I know...........who wants AI in a simulation racer.  Let's be honest, there isn't a racing sim out there that can compete with the online community of iRacing.  You ALWAYS find human racers to compete with.  That's not to say that Automobilista doesn't have a mulitplayer community.  Indeed, you can log on and find some multiplayer races.  However, the community has not expanded yet.  Therefore, you NEED AI to get some traffice time it.  The scaleable AI here is some of the best I've seen in a racing sim yet.  They truly try to find the best path around you for a pass and seem to attempt to avoid all contact.
5.  Complaints. As I said earlier, this is an early access of the game.  However, I want to be sure to let everyone know if some of the downsides that I think exists.  First, you will notice some clipping when you collide with certain artifacts in the game.  It's nothing that ruins the overall realism and fun of the sim, however, it's there. Also, there seems to be some scaling issues with a few of the tracks. Montreal's straights seem to be pretty short.  Speaking of tracks, there are curently 0 American Road  Courses in the game.  Hopefully this will change..........(Long Beach, St Petersburg......FORGET Laguna Seca).  There are also a lot of tracks that are either new to me or not real world tracks.  When setting up a single player practice session, you have to manually add the AI cars..............ONE CAR AT A TIME.....CLICK.....CLICK.....CLICK.... Hopefully this will get changed.
6.  Speaking of cars............There are several in here that are not mainstream to your typcial racer.  COPA is something complete new to me.............and I love it.  COPA MONTANA are GT trucks that are pretty damn fun to drive.  The other COPA (sorry cannot remember the spelling or name) is GT Hondas Civics and Cheverolets.  Pretty damn fun to run these rice burners.  There are also SUPER V8 TRUCKS and tracks (imaging dirt rally truck on a race track with buitl in jumps).  Definitely a change of pace.  What doesn't exist right now are true GT3/GT1 cars.
All in all, I'm really excited to see what Reiza is going to do with this simulation.  They have definitely come out swinging and are directly challenging the mainstream racing simulations on the market today.  This is how you do an early access game here........(hint hint hiht Star Citizen).  Looking forward to more to come.  I'll update this review as new content comes out.

The Good:
Custom Weapons: You make them yourself from a huge list of unlockable parts so it's easy to create something unique to you and which suits your play style (unlike the weaponcrafting for some games the developers haven't just made use of a load of paint jobs to make it look like there's more options than there actually are).
Game Balance: When playing online with strangers you're grouped together based on your in game exp meaning that you don't get matches between one team of really experienced players and one of complete novices.
No pay to win: The only way to improve weapons/get ahead is through playing the game (the only things you can buy for real world money are outfits for your avatar which are just cosmetic).
Match Type tweaks: You've got the bog standard MP game modes (TD, CTF, CP) but they've been twisted so they feel quite fresh, e.g. in the CTF mode the flag can be used as a weapon to increase your team's capture score by killing enemies with it.
Variety: Unlike some games (say TF2) where some maps exist solely for one game type, every single map can be used to play any game type so there's plenty of variety in terms of gameplay.
Price: It's free, so that's a plus!
The Bad:
Lack of Game modes: There's only 5 of them (6 if you count the mash up used in ranked matches)
Maps: There's only about 5 maps (well 10 technically but half of them are the same maps with different lighting)
Repetitiveness: See above
The Meh:
There's nothing in the game that makes me want to say: "OMG! YOU NEED TO PLAY THIS!"
Overall verdict:
Decent game with some nice features but nothing that really makes it stand out from the crowd. Worth getting since it's free and a good (and fun) way of spending a few hours.

I was looking for an RPG, one with aspects like loot, adventure, sci-fi, multiple endings, etc. and was just not finding it at all. All the games I had heard of and had played were starting to bore me. That's when my dad suggested I play the Fallout series.
At this point in my life, we only had Macs in our house, and Bethesda only released Fallout for Windows. So, I searched and searched, but I couldn't find a Mac version that worked for new computers. Eventually, I got a Dell to do some game programming, then I found out I could download Fallout on Steam. I immediately did, and loved it.
It has the perfect blend of RPG, adventure, sci-fi, even some western and fantasy aspects, as well as strategy, turn-based combat, and more. The multiple endings had me at least playing over and over to save certain people, or to kill others. Keep in mind that it is an old game, so it definitely has some graphics issues, but they don't affect anything. I highly reccommend this game to anyone looking for a game that encorperates a great plot, decent graphics, and strategic turn-based combat.

Let me make this clear from the start, this is not a controller meant to replace a keyboard/mouse nor is it a competitor with standard controllers. This is a device intended for people with autism and as such only benefits people who are autistic enough to make full use of it. If you are a normalfag you will not enjoy this controller, it'll likely only serve to irritate you before you trash it.
I've been using the controller exclusively for several days now and its really grown on me. The trackpads felt very nice to use and generally did a decent job emulating a mouse. I've tried a number of titles on the device and it does a appreciable job all around, just so long as you take the time to get it set up perfectly. Don't use the community configs, they're near useless. You need to set it up yourself if you want to get the most out of it. That's what I mean when I say the controller is meant for autistic people, it requires dedication and an obsessive amount of time to get down. If you think you're able to do it then I'd recommend it, the moment of satisfaction when you get the perfect config set up is pure bliss.
Build wise the controller is solid, It feels very comfortable to hold. It didn't feel cheap, despite the official reviews done on the product (by people who aren't autistic clearly). The standard controls (buttons, analog stick, triggers etc.) feel high quality, the analog stick especially feels a lot more comfortable to use than the xbox 360 controller I was accustomed to. This was a device meant for big guys, if you're a big guy then this is the controller for you.
Does this feel better than an xbox controller or whatever you plug into your computer? Purely subjective but I prefered the steam controller over my old one. I found it to not just be a controller but a tool as well, I could lounge back while looking at websites and the controller seems to be perfect for playing visual novels, mostly because you can play them with one hand.
The only problems I had with it were the lack of decent rumble, the haptic rumble emulation really isn't that good, and that pitiful excuse for a dpad. They really should have just made both pads the same and got rid of that asinine groove. It feels weird and doesn't have any of the qualities of a d-pad. Its absolutely useless.
9/10 for autistic people like myself
4/10 for a normalfag

This is a fun game where you can disassemble and reassemble guns, take them into a firing range, find out it's history, etc. You unlock guns with 'experience', which is earned by completing the various game modes with the current guns you have. The first time you complete a mode, you get a nice chunk of experience, which is dependent on how far along the gun tree you are. The further you are, the more experience you get.
You can also get experience by completing various challenges for each gun, such as doing a full disassemble and reassemble within a certain timeframe, and/or doing it without any mistakes. These also net you a good chunk of experience the first time you do it, and for the consequent times you do it, while it won't be as much as the first, still rewards you with a decent amount.
You do need to grind a bit later on to get more guns, but by the time you get to the real grindy bits, you'll have a large variety of guns to mess with, so it shouldn't be tedious.
Obviously, that all depends on how much you're interested in guns. For those who are interested, this will hold your attention for quite a while. If you're specifically interested on how guns are disassembled and reassembled, and would enjoy doing so like I am, then this is the game for you and you won't even notice the grind, since what you'd be doing for fun would be a grind to someone who isn't as interested.
And, of course, you can buy the weapons, including all of them at once. Personally, that takes away all the fun. The weapons are very much attainable without spending a dime. Those who complain about 'pay-2-unlock' are people who only have a passing interest in guns, or have very little interest in disassembly, but still expect everything from this game for free.
Overall, this is a great game people who love disassembling guns. It has a very fair unlocking system, and if you want to support the devs, or get your favorite gun ASAP, you can use real money to do so. You can just unlock everything with one payment though, if you dislike fun.
Also, they claim to be adding a new gun at least once a month. Seeing as it's only been out for 3 days at the time of this review, I think we should give them some time.

This is a shooter that a lot of other shooters should take notes from.
Additionally the map creater system is easy to use and allows for creation of some pretty fun maps.
My only negative is a partial one towards the multiplayer. Graphics maintain well and gunplay remains pretty much the same. Strangely this doesn't entirely translate well I think mostly because the style is too familiar and the game doesn't offer any particularly unique game mode to stand apart. This isn't to say it is bad, it just isn't the point I could sell this game on as it offers nothing unique for FPS games.
Overall my scoring would be 9.5/10 with the half point demotion for the well done but non-unique multiplayer. Everything else from gameplay, graphics, music, story and map creater I give this game great credit for and highly recommend its purchase.

This is my first ever Steam review :)
I have played many games in the past. This is the first game that evoked such strong emotion from me that after finishing it, I used chapter select to go back and finish the many quests that I ignored in the first playthrough. And I savored every little interaction between the main characters during these quests.
The only other experience comparable to this one that I can recall was playing through FF7, MGS1, and watching Neon Genesis Evangelion. But back then I was still a teenager so I was easily impressed. Now I'm in my thirties.
One thing that I regret was letting the costume design and fan-service aspect of the game mislead me into underestimate the game initially. What I had dismissed as lazy-writing and cliched dialogues during some of the scenes turned out to be pure gold.
The mechanics aspects of the games are far from flawless, as many review sites will tell you, but to me, judging this game based on things like how much it scores in the graphics or music department (which is epic) is completely missing the point. Nonetheless, I do want to mention one technical point of the game that completely blew my mind:  the animation of the female characters. Such elegance, style, and beauty. Hats off to the mocap actors and animators. If this cannot be called art, I don't know what can.
To summarize, this is a game that transcends the norms, and pushes games as an (albeti young) art form forward. It will be a yardstick that future titles will copy from and be compared against.
I fully completed the story of this game and I can't get it out of my head. 9.5/10 would recommend.

I've been a fan of the series since jumping in as Frank West chasing a story and sadly the game has never had as an interesting character as Frank. I believe the game is alright, but I wouldn't rate it too highly.
The Good:
-Great crafting mechanic. A bit hilarious with some of the combos, but some very destructive and fun combos
-Lots of endless zombies!
-A large open world that feels like a real city
-More than enough time for missions
-Levelling up gives you the ability to substitude parts that are similar as well as a choice.
-Safe houses give you the ability to regain weapons you've either crafted or items you've picked up so you can combine them.
-The plot is interesting, but dissappointing in some aspects, which I won't spoil here.
The Bad:
-Due to roadblocks, which do make for some creative ways of travel, can be a real pain when you need to get to the third area from the 1st.
-The bad-end exploration where you find people who killed themselves it plays a depressing music tune, but you get aweful puns like someone who set themselves on fire and it says "They couldn't stand the heat." or other stupid lines which don't reflect the music, nor the character's reaction and comes off like a kid trying to use dark humour.
-When I was first playing the game I had no idea how to get rid of Survivors. In pervious games, you simply brought them back to the safehouse as the idea was you were trying to get survivors out of the area or, in the case of Dead Rising 2, hole up in a bunker until the military sweep up. Here, survivors are 2 types. Ones who you save and run off, earning you PP whilst others tag along with you like old games, but that is their main use. As backup muscle and it's never explained how to remove them from the party.
The Ugly:
-Though there aren't any issues with graphics normally, there is often a terrible "pop-in" effect where everything is low rez for a few seconds and then cleans itself up.
-This will be hit or miss with people but most of the character's themselves are rarther bland and i never really felt a sense of urgency when they were in danger. I felt about as concerned as Willy Wonka "No, stop, come back.
-for me there's not enough to warrent a second playthrough unless you are one of those people who needs 100% completeion. Besides from that there's really no other reason.
Overall I'd recommend this game on a discount, but certainly not the full price as I don't feel it quite justifies it.

So i've just finished this game and want to give a review:
First of all it's overall a pretty solid shooter game with really nice graphics and sound. The pace of the game is fast (unlike the Doom 3 protagonist who felt as slow as a guy in a wheelchair).
What I liked:
- All the original monsters from the real Doom games (part 3 excluded) are there and they feel basically like them.
- The original weapons find a place in this game and they even put some on top.
- The gore level is what I would expect from a Doom game and it delivered.
- The pacing of the game is fast even though sometimes I was kinda missing a sprint key.
- The story is sufficient enough to give me a second motivation to kill them all (the first motivation is pretty obvious with a Doom game I think)
What bothered me:
For me Bethesda is the 80% company: They have some really nice games in their portfolio and those I played I really liked. But it feels like they are never really giving it the final polish that a game would need to become really great. I see this in Fallout and Skyrim but the fantastic modding support more than redeems that. In this game though I don't see the same modding potential and that brings me to the following list:
- The game is short. I guess there is no need to sugar-coat that fact.
- Weapon upgrades are not a bad idea in general but in this game I think it takes the wrong implementation. To REALLY upgrade all the weapons in the game you need to find a buttload of secrets or have to do special challenges with the respective weapon to unlock the highest tier upgrade.
Personally I see the necessity to upgrade my weapons as much as I can to unlock their true potential. Too bad though that I found myself breaking the flow of the game and roaming around the empty maps after killing everything afterwards. In a game like that this is NOT wnat I want to do.
The weapon challenges are especially annoying when you have to do something to a special kind of enemy that is not overly present in the current map or is surrounded by other enemy types that block you from quickly achieving this challenge.
- To the above mentions point comes that I think there are way too few enemies in the game. I played on the easiest setting after getting my♥♥♥♥♥handed by the enemies in the first maps on a higher difficulty due to their bullet sponginess and extreme damage output. I think this is very Doom-unlike.
- In my opinion there should be enemies that are as strong as on the second hardest setting but more.. way more.
- I was shocked to see how pathetic the DOOM-guy was in the first maps. Just 20 shotgun shells and you have to get really, really close to kill an Imp.. c'mon.
- In later maps (and after scrounding alot for secrets :/) I became almost godlike which made fight too easy. You don't have this in the original Doom games and it should not have been included in here.
- Calling this game just "DOOM".... I mean really. Everyone knows that MicroSoft cannot cound correctly, but I expected more from you guys. Don't listen to the marketing monkeys. I know that monkeys through feces around when they want to demonstrate dominance but that doesn't mean you have to catch it all and re-use it.
All in all I would have given this game a higher rating if it was a bit more like the original Doom games in a better graphics but i'm still willing to give it a 7/10.

One of the best sandbox-style games I've ever played! Bully beautifully weaves tweaked Grand Theft Auto gameplay with the universally relatable life story of young Jimmy Hopkins. The setting of a fictional New England boarding school and the nearby town of Bullworth are perfect for this kind of story, following Jimmy as he faces the same challenges that every kid faces growing up, like keeping up with schoolwork, fighting back against bullies, experiencing your first kiss, causing chaos through pranks and hijinks, and finding acceptance between various cliques and social groups.
The writing is brilliant, supplying a colorful cast of characters, missions, and story arcs. Including Jimmy himself, all of the NPCs seem practically handcrafted with the amount of personality and detail put into them. Each character has a unique model, and their own unique set of dialogues and animations. On top of these fantastically created characters, the plot is just as good. I was immersed into a world that I could have sworn was from an 80's Hollywood flick, drawing inspiration from coming-of-age tales like those of Sixteen Candles, The Breakfast Club, and Catcher in the Rye. With such a wonderfully realistic world full of jocks, preps, nerds, and other odd townfolk, I almost wish that my own school days growing up were as interesting as those of Bullworth Academy.
The gameplay is just as entertaining, using similar mechanics to GTA, such as a wanted system (called Truancy, of course), a combat system filled with a diverse array of punches, throws, and weapons at your disposal, different vehicles, mini-games, and other various activities and collectibles for completionists. As usual, there are missions given by various NPCs, some advancing the main story, and others being small side activities. Camera angles can be strange at times, but I've never experienced any gamebreaking issues with it. Overall, the gameplay has enough variance where it doesn't get too repetitive, and it strikes a nice balance that makes it both interesting and easy to pick up.
Compared to other open-world games, Bully is by far my favorite. One of the few titles I've been compelled to complete 100%. If you're looking for something different in the same vein of games such as Grand Theft Auto, Saints Row, and the like, I highly recommend looking into Bully: Scholarship Edition. You won't be disappointed.

When I saw this had become available on Steam, I was overjoyed. Freespace: The Great War was one of my absolute favorite games as a child, and I believe it still holds up strongly to this day.
The game begins 14 years into the war between the Terrans and Vasudans, and before long, an even greater threat shows its face, an ancient and destructive alien race known only as the Shivans...enemy to Terran and Vasudan alike.
Freespace: The Great War is a space flight sim. While most missions involve you either protecting an important target, or wiping out enemy forces, oftentimes both, they are all varied in their actual content and no two missions really feel the same. As the game progresses, you gain access to a good variety of different ships, each with varying strengths and weaknesses, as well as an assortment of different weapons.
Another of Freespace's strong points is its atmosphere, formed mostly from the music and dialogue. It will make you feel like you ARE the pilot, and a part of the game itself. This is definitely one of the things that helps to set Freespace apart from other space sims. I have never played another space sim that gave quite the same feeling Freespace does.
This release includes the expansion, Silent Threat, which continues the story after the main campaign's ending with several additional missions.
I really can't recommend this game enough. If you're a fan space flight sims or flight sims in general, and have not played this game, now's your chance to experience a masterpiece.

For those on the fence because Automobilista uses what some describe as a dated physics and graphics engine, the answer is that does not matter at all. The team at Reiza UNDERSTAND what it takes to make a satisfying sim, and no amount of slick graphics (Project Cars) substitute for engaging driving and gameplay. Let's take the setup of the cars and the physics:
Reiza has refined and tweaked the ISI engine so that almost every car available gives wonderful feedback to the driver. You can feel when you are on the edge, and this is down to not only the beautifully tweaked physics but very importantly the customisable sounds including tyres and various balance controls enables you to get a very good idea of how fast you can push. Every clue that you need, both in sound and feedback, is customisable and exceedingly well done, including rumble strips, grass and dirt, and for me this is the only sim which offers believable reactions to being offline or offtrack. It also makes it much easier than other sims to catch a slide because you can feel what is happening to the back end of the car.
Frankly I do not care whether the graphics are not to PCars "standard". Most of those are in any case a distraction from the job in hand: racing. The cars are very well done and despite not being fleshed out with bling like PCars are still perfectly good and crucially are way ahead in practical driving terms.
The force feedback is (again unlike Project Cars with its frankly ludicrously complex FF setup - which doesn't have any clear explanations as to what the absurd number of parameters mean) simple yet highly effective.
The AI in Automobilista is outstanding and superior to ANY currently available racing sim, yet Reiza are still working to refine it. This makes it by far the most satisfying offline racing experience.
The one slight misgiving is the available tracks. It's not because they are mostly Brazilian circuits or somewhat unfamiliar, but that many of them are rather plain looking and consist often of very wide tracks with long, shallow or sweeping curves. Some make like these but I find them a bit samey and lacking in character. However I think Reiza Studios recognise this and are encouraging third party circuits and perhaps in the future will offer some classic tracks.
Overall this is a very promising sim and despite being early access is already close to being a very polished product. Even at this stage it is far more polished and playable than either PCars or Assetto. It is also far more polished and offers much better quality content than ISI whose own content in rfactor 2 is falling way behind.

Rampage Knights starts with a short cutscene involving two men sitting around a campfire. These two men are brave heroes back from their latest adventure! They're lost in a forest so they decide to rest until sunrise and set out again but before they can do that, a strange figure arises from the bonfire. It looks like the face of a person who wore the Majora's Mask if it took a toll on your health and sanity and horribly disfigured you. The figure is a Warlock who steals the heroes hard earned treasures and while the heroes try to fight back, the warlock subdues them easily. The heroes later wake up in the middle of a camp and that is where the game begins...
Once you're in control of the player, you soon realize that you're surrounded by many strangers who seem to have the abilities to help you in some way, except for Tim the Alchemist. He seems pointless with that cauldron of his. This is the central hub for the rest of the game, where you'll practice your moves, change classes, and change outfits. The only way out is through the forest, but the forest is full of monsters and only leads to a nearby castle, presumably where the warlock resides with your treasure.
Classes are unlocked through completing certain achievements during your runs, most likely related to the class in some way. There are 6 different classes to choose from and you only start with the very first class called Adventurer. Adventurer has no unique traits and is considered average in every way. Other classes will have unique abilities or traits such as the Barbarian who has more vitality and wields a Final Fantasy 7-esque longsword that has an insanely long reach but the downside is that a Barbarian cannot wear armour. The Pirate class has a peg leg, starts with a pet parrot that attacks enemies and regains health while drunk. Assassins can one-shot enemies lying on the ground and uses smokescreens to avoid attacks. Warlocks can summon demons and Battlemages can use multiple magic attacks and Teleportation.
Before you can set out, there's a short tutorial section to the left of where you begin. A notebook explains the mechanics of the game on screen in short and simple terms. X is to attack, you can chain combos depending on the way you move your thumbstick and the distance your enemy is before you. If an enemy is extremely close to you, you can push kick them which knocks them back and on to the ground. Once enemies are on the ground you can either pick them up or stomp on them for major damage. You can charge up your weapon for sweeping attacks, sweeps and aerial combos both break shields. There are also four item slots used for magic, throwable weapons, scrolls and potions. That's about all the basics to learn! Now you're armed with the knowledge to kick some monster tail.
Right at the entrance of the forest is a jester with the option of changing the difficulty setting. The default setting is Normal Mode, there are four difficulty settings ranging from Casual to Insane Mode. On Normal, permadeath is activated which means once you die you have to start over completely from the beginning of the game and losing all items and weapons. Casual Mode disables permadeath allowing you to restart at the last level you died if you're afraid of losing your progression. This allows even non roguelike fans to enjoy Rampage Knights as I know some players don't enjoy the aspect of starting over from nothing over and over again.
I feel that Rampage Knights plays best with a friend, while I played solo for a bit, it was when I coop'd online with a friend of mine that I truly felt like I was having a blast. The gameplay consists of moving room to room clearing out enemies that can range from a few skeleton warriors to mobs of demons and giant Orc minibosses. When you play solo, it can be easy to get flanked by hordes of enemies from every direction on higher difficulties. With another player at your side you can spread the aggro into a pincer style battle formation, making it much harder for enemies to get the jump on you. If one of you dies, the player becomes a ghost that can help stun enemies and can be revived by receiving a certain number of souls from killed enemies. Throughout the rooms you will find lots of treasure chests, these chests are unlocked using a minigame very similar to the lockpicking one in Elder Scrolls Oblivion where you push tumblers in a pattern except that if you fail it will do physical damage to your character.
These chests usually contain money which allows you to buy rare items from vendors but chances are they will also drop weapons like a generic battle axe or even the Mjolnir itself which shoots astral hammers. They can also drop rare items that can boost your attributes or give you special abilities. Monsters can also drop loot that may give you demon like powers such as familiars that can shoot giant laser beams or fire breath. This is where the game truly feels at it's best, the weapons you can find have so many different effects. You can find weird weapons that are weak but summon giant pillars that rain death on your enemies or even yourself if you're not careful. There are also Altars which contain magic orbs that will give you abilities that consume mana such as teleportation or chain lightning. Combine this with all the different armour slots and you get a huge variation of abilities and skills during each run that are drastically different. You can get cursed or diseased by drinking potions, making deals with devils, or even altar sacrifices which usually 'reward' you with perks of some kind like double jump, or permanent strength boost but the downside is that you may end up with an♥♥♥♥♥for a head or worse, every single inanimate object in every room is now an enemy you have to defeat.
Overall Rampage Knights is a fun beat em up game that is best played with a friend. With multiple difficulties it accommodates many different levels of players, even allowing pearmadeath to be disabled. With so many outfits to unlock you'll always be able to slay monsters in style. With so many different weapons and builds to experiment with, it's easy to do multiple runs and lose track of time. I highly recommend this to gamers who want a fun multiplayer or couch coop experience similar to Castle Crashers but with a lot more variety in weapons and loot.

Rampage Knights is an excellent and polished game with plenty of humor, or references, to spare! The finest game from "Rake in Grass" yet! It is an excellent blend of beat 'em up and RPG!
Here's a summary of the Positives (+) and Negatives (-):
+ Tons of weapons, items, and abilities all on a randomized loot table. You'll never know what kind of combonation you'll get!
+ Nearly infinite replay value. All levels are randomized, and feature other sorts of surprises you won't experience twice in a row.
+ Fun and rewarding combat that is easy to get into, but hard to master.
+ Very challenging!
+ Colorful and detailed 2D visuals.
+ Great soundtrack!
+ Singleplayer or co-op, offline or on.
+ Achievements that actually matter! Earn them to gain greater strenth and cool passive bonuses. It can even unlock classes to play as.
+/- Not enough boss encounters. There are only TWO bosses... however, one of these bosses is on a randomization table, and you'll sometimes get a completely different boss!
- Animations and sprites are often copy/paste across multiple enemies.
- Jump attacks are too overpowered... in true Golden Axe fashion!
- Friendly fire is annoying in co-op games!
Akward at first, Amazing in the end. Can be fine tuned to do so many things. It is up to the task. Solid purchase.

The haptics in the controller make the scroll of the trackpad feel mechanical and good under your thumbs. It feels like there is a trackball inside the controller.
What I enjoy the most from this controller is the complete customization this controller has. Every input can be manipulated. You can  lock one track pad to a part of the screen for mini map controls and the other for main inputs. I love tinkering with settings on PC games and this extends that tinkering to the controller. There is also a community feature where you can download bindings that other steam users have made for an individual game. I have done the same for Mass Effect and it's such a great feeling when you see that other people are using your bindings!

I highly recommend this game, I however do /not/ recommend the official server. The official server is filled with bots, a terrible cash shop, and a not so great community. This is a great game, but you will enjoy it far more if you play on the private server, Aurakingdom.to. The rest of this review will be referring to my experiences in the private server.
One thing that really ruins the official server is the rampant population of bots run by gold sellers. The market in the OS is terrible because of this, with the auction house having terrible prices because of the availability of gold sellers. The private server has a non-intrusive captcha, which pops up if you kill world mobs, or collect resources. It doesn't pop up when you are fishing however, so you can still afk fish without worrying. This does a great job at dealing with bots, in fact I haven't seen a single bot on the private server in all the time I've been on. Gold sellers are pretty much non-existant in the private server, and the  auction house is far fairer in pricing.
The official server is also has a very bad cash shop. The private server's cash shop is far fairer, and you can get by without the cash shop easily. Aura kingdom has a section of the item mall known as the paragon table, where for 200 ruby coins you can roll for the first level of a multi-tier lottery table. If you don't get the emerald coins, which are one slot on the table row, you can advance to the next row, which has better items. You will lose the chance to get the item you landed on, but you get a chance at better items. This continues until you choose to stick with the item you landed on, or you land on the emerald coins. The emerald coins can be used to start your roll on a higher level if you have enough of them built up. The OS paragon tables are bad, and what you'd expect from a company such as Aeria. Aurakingdom.to's paragon tables are far more generous, and allow you to get nice cosmetics far more easily. For instance, at the time of writing this, the private server just released an update with new mounts, and the paragon table is filled with mounts, pets, and mount ability re-shuffle scrolls.
The private server also gives you 12 ap every day that you are online for 3 hours or more, which is a nice way to make a little AP over time. Additionally, the loyalty shop is far more generous in what it provides, with more permanent costumes (there really aren't many trial costumes available in the loyalty shop, which is a good thing). So, my point here is that Aeria is greedy and has implemented their usual terrible cash shop in the official server, and the private server is far more generous and fair in what they provide.
Content that has been implemented in the official server is very far behind compared to what is released overseas, this is not a problem in the private server, as the private server is far more up to date in what content they have. For instance, recently around a week ago the PS released the update the upped the lvl cap to 99. The only downside to this is that there is some content that is not translated yet, but is still available in the private server. I don't really view this as a problem, as it's something that will get fixed in time as the PS team works on translating, and it isn't really a huge hindrance.
Another thing that made me quit the official server was how grindy the game got over time, past lvl 40 the game slows down and leveling is very slow. To make matters worse, in order to advance into the lvl 60 zones, you have to complete 3 lvl 55 zones, which each are basically the same thing over again each time. Now, once you get to lvl 60, leveling is a lot more fun as you can run a lot of the dungeons now, but getting there is a slow monotonous experience. The private server has increased exp rates, which largely fixes this problem, it is much easier to get to the lvl 60 zones, and it doesn't take too long to get there either. The private server gets you into the fun content much faster, and fixes the issues with quest grinding the official server suffers from.
Finally, the private server has a very nice community! From my experiences, the community is very welcoming, and if you hop onto the private server discord channel, or even world chat people are very willing to provide you with tips on how to build your character. I've had nothing but good experiences in my interactions with people on the private server, and they are very welcoming to new players.
So tl;dr,
The official server is plagued by Aeria's terrible policies, lots of bots and gold sellers, a bad community, and grindy leveling past lvl 40.
The private server fixes these issues, and is a lot more enjoyable to play on.
If you want to play the game, which I highly recommend, play on the private server and you'll have a lot more fun

I have been playing with the Steam Controller for about a month at the time of this publishing.
First things first: fully remappable buttons, trackpads, a joystick, and two buttons on the back.
I'm not gonna go out of my way to praise this product just because it's a Steam product. A lot of people are probably very excited that Vavle is making hardware, and they probably won't think of anything else but the product and how they think it's superior only because Valve made it.
With that being said: This controller isn't anywhere near what I thought it would be...
...but it's not uncomfortable.
The thing about this controller is that it's not a replacement for whatever controller you regularly use on your PC. It's to be used for games that don't have gamepad support, and for using the computer from far away (think Steam Machines and Steam Link).
Another thing that takes a bit of getting used to is the placement of the joystick, abxy buttons, and trackpad.
On an XBONE controller (which is what I used until it died and I decided to try the Steam Controller) the left joystick is at the top left of the gamepad, and the d-pad on the lower left of the game pad. The right joystick is at the bottom right, and the abxy buttons on the top right.
On the steam controller however, the left joystick is at the bottom left, the d-pad on the top left, the right trackpad/joystick is on the top right and the abxy buttons on the bottom right.
So everything is just kind of switched around.
If you think you'll like it, you probably will, but some aspects might disappoint you. and if you think you won't like it then don't get it, it really isn't THAT great.
Neat, not the most comfortable but not offputting, joysticks/d-pad/abxybuttons switched up, almost feels like a prototype. It's cool to use the computer on a TV from far away, and some games actually play very nicely on the Steam Controller. I've been playing a lot of Rocket League with it and it's great. Also worked very nicely when I booted up Dragon's Dogma.
But anyways, I'm not really making this a full on review, I just wanted to let people know what I thought about the controller.

This is a feature-driven product that allows for a ton of customizations/configurations for what might currently be a small niche of gamers.  It is not a performance or ease-of-use driven product, however, and for all the features it offers it makes little difference when simply holding the device is so awkward and counterintuitive. For someone with small hands, the buttons are hard to reach, for those with larger hands, your thumbs will likely be touching due to the the ridiculously small area designated to the stick and ABXY buttons.  I look to controllers more for performance and ease-of-use than I do for unlimited configurations and fun-but-unnecessary features.  A decent remote touchpad, if that's what you're looking for, but it's sold as a full-on game controller, and it's not a very good one of those.

Rampage Knights is an awesome rogue-like dungeon crawler. You choose your class (bad: you can only play as one class in the beginning) and go into the dungeon. There you beat up monsters, find items and defeat the final boss - or die.
Though it may seem very hard to play at the start, as soon as you figured out some of the game mechanics it becomes really funny and easy to play. And even if you die 10 times in the first level - hell, it´s a roguelike game, what did you expect?
You make progression by completing challenges, for example dealing a certain amount of magical damage. By completing a challenge, you get a permanent boost for your character (like more magical damage), unlock a new character class, a higher difficulty etc. Simple and good.
Let´s move over to the cons now. It is very easy to die in this game, and playing coop will sure test your friendship for you can not damage your friends, but still send them up flying and stop their attacks. The hitboxes of enemies and yourself are pretty strange sometimes, but it is not that much to worry about. The only thing I really disliked was that after 16 hours in coop with my friend (I count myself and him as casual games), we unlocked about 80% of all unlockable content and are currently trying to beat the game on the highest difficulty. There are no new items or weapons anymore, we know them all. The only thing to do for us is to simply hope for the best drop luck - there is nothing new anymore.
To conclude, I say that if you like rogue-like games and don´t mind comic-styled graphics, this game is definetely worth a try. It lacks a bit of content, but you can still have your 20 or 25 hours fun with it. Go ahead and try. I really like it.
